title: Soil and vegetation water content identify the main terrestrial ecosystem changes
data: microwave L-band soil moisture and vegetation optical depth, land cover change maps
method: trend mapping of soil and vegetation water content, attribution of change by clustering with land cover change, greenness and precipitation
predictors: land cover change, vegetation greenness, precipitation variability
finding: Trends of minus 8 to 9 per cent a year in soil and vegetation water content, 2010 to 2020, clustered by driver, including deforestation in the Amazon and Central Africa.
gap_quote: How vegetation responds to natural and human activity still needs to be well established, quantified and understood.

title: Spatio-temporal Monitoring of Deforestation Using Polarimetric Radar Imagery from Sentinel-1 Satellite: Case of the Ebo Forest, Littoral Region, Cameroon: Deforestation Using Polarimetric Radar Imagery from Sentinel-1 Satellite.
data: Sentinel-1 polarimetric radar classification
method: random forest, support vector machine and k-nearest neighbours classification
validation: accuracy assessment, reference data not stated
measures: overall accuracy above 93 per cent for random forest
finding: Dense forest fell from 87 to 73 per cent of the Ebo Forest from 2017 to 2025, a net loss near 210 square kilometres, mostly in the north and southeast.
gap_quote: The study highlights the added value of radar imagery in detecting gradual forest degradation under canopy, where optical sensors often fail.

title: National forest cover change baselines for six countries of the Congo basin using open-source solutions and sample-based area estimates (2015–2023)
data: satellite data with sample-based area estimates
method: sample-based area estimation with statistically derived confidence intervals, attribution of direct drivers
predictors: small-scale agriculture, artisanal forestry, industrial forestry
validation: statistically validated sample-based estimates, design not stated
finding: Deforestation in six Congo Basin countries was largely stable from 2015 to 2023, while degradation grew in some, driven mainly by small-scale agriculture and artisanal and industrial forestry.
gap_quote: With a rapidly growing human population and both local and international demand for natural resources, the threats to these forests are expected to increase.

title: Climate Change Mitigation: Should “Avoided Deforestation” Be Rewarded?
data: not stated
method: not stated
finding: Argues against rewarding avoided deforestation because ex ante baselines are inaccurate and ex post baselines lack legitimacy, likely yielding fake reductions, and favours existing governance instruments instead.
gap_quote: Several proposals were designed for such a mechanism, yet their implementation poses significant methodological problems: first, sophisticated tools available to measure the reduction of emissions might be ineffective when combined with baselines on a national level; secondly, baselines calculated ex ante lack accuracy because of insufficient knowledge concerning the direct and underlying causes of deforestation

title: Quantified soil dynamics and spatial fragmentation within the shifting agricultural landscape in southern Cameroon
data: multispectral satellite imagery classification
method: conceptual model of shifting agriculture with transition matrices, multi-criteria selection of soil properties, fractional rational function models, image classification
validation: accuracy assessment, reference data not stated
finding: Land use explained 30 to 35 per cent of topsoil variance, five soil properties were most sensitive, and imagery mapped the shifting agriculture front with 80 per cent accuracy.

title: Land Use and Land Cover Dynamics in the Eseka Alluvial Gold Mining District, Centre Region, Cameroon
place: Cameroon, Centre Region, Eseka alluvial gold mining district
data: Landsat classification
method: Landsat image classification, ground truthing of agents and drivers
predictors: farming, wood extraction, alluvial gold mining, economic motives
validation: accuracy assessment, reference data not stated
finding: Forest fell from 98 to 34 per cent of the district from 1990 to 2022, a loss near 98,263 hectares, attributed to farming, wood extraction and alluvial gold mining.
gap_quote: The exploitation of these resources invariably leads to deforestation and forest degradation.

title: Modeling the Impact of Landscape Dynamics on Soil Erosion in Eastern DR Congo: Implications for Sustainable Land Management
place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kalehe territory
data: Landsat classification
method: revised universal soil loss equation in GIS, supervised classification, Pearson correlation, principal component analysis, multiple linear regression
predictors: landscape composition indices, landscape structure metrics, deforestation, landscape diversity, fragmentation, patch shape complexity, patch size
finding: Soil erosion rose from 32.08 to 44.35 tonnes per hectare a year from 1987 to 2020, rising with deforestation, landscape diversity and fragmentation, and falling with patch size and complexity.
gap_quote: However, there is limited information about the spatiotemporal dynamic of soil erosion under different conditions of LULC changes in mountainous regions of eastern DR Congo.

title: Preliminary estimation of carbon stock in a logging concession with a forest management plan in East Cameroon
place: Cameroon, East Cameroon, one forest management unit
data: field inventory of the annual allowable cut
method: aboveground biomass from tree inventory, carbon tracked from felling to sawmill and export
finding: Of 6.78 tonnes of carbon per hectare inventoried, 1.84 were logged and 0.32 reached export, while logging damage affected 4.45 per cent of the cut, almost 33,188 tonnes of carbon.
gap_quote: These findings show that the implementation of reduced-impact logging (RIL) could reduce these losses throughout the logging steps and help propose a process for the valuation of wood waste in the forest and sawmill.

title: Remote carbon cycle changes are overlooked impacts of land cover and land management changes
data: hypothetical global cropland expansion, irrigation and afforestation scenarios
method: sensitivity simulations with three Earth system models, checkerboard land cover perturbation
finding: Nonlocal carbon effects of simulated land cover change altered terrestrial carbon stock by 1 to 37 gigatonnes over 160 years, including 0.3 to 15 in the central Congo Basin.
gap_quote: Given that the terrestrial carbon cycle strongly depends on climate conditions, this raises the question of whether LCLMCs can trigger remote carbon cycle changes (nonlocal BGC effects) – a currently overlooked, potentially large climate and ecosystem impact.

title: Economic activities and deforestation in the Congo basin: An environmental kuznets curve framework analysis
data: World Bank and FAO national statistics
method: fixed and random effects panel regression, Hausman test
predictors: agriculture, gross domestic product, manufacturing, population, openness, forest rents, institutions
finding: Agriculture, gross domestic product, population, openness, forest rents and institutions were significant determinants of deforestation, with a U-shaped relation to economic activity, inverted only for manufacturing.
gap_quote: We contribute to this literature by estimating the aggregated and disaggregated effects of economic activities on deforestation in the Congo Basin, a region that has experienced an increase in deforestation in recent years.

title: Deforestation Impacts on Biodiversity Conservation in the Dja Biosphere Reserve of Cameroon
data: not stated
method: qualitative analysis of selected data and policies against management theories
finding: The reserve remained 90 per cent untouched, but some species were endangered, threats were rising, and local households relied on it for subsistence and income.
gap_quote: Despite the fact that this area is a natural reserve implying that certain human activities like cutting down of forests around the buffer zones and hunting without permission are outlawed, we notice that there is increasing damage being done to this reserve especially around its periphery.

title: Mitigating the impact of bad rainy seasons in poor agricultural regions to tackle deforestation
data: high-resolution remotely sensed annual tree cover loss and land cover
method: not stated
predictors: seasonal rainfall quality, proportion of agricultural land, remoteness, human activity, land cover
finding: A short rainy season raised deforestation by 15 per cent in forested areas and 20 per cent in unconnected areas with little cropland, in poor rainfed farming regions.
gap_quote: However, in addition to the direct effect of climate change on forest biomes, recent sparse evidence has shown that land use changes may increase as a result of weather shocks.

title: Parcel-Level Deforestation Hazard Rates in the Paraguayan Chaco: A Multi-Scale Empirical Analysis of Annual Clearing Dynamics on Large Cattle Ranches
data: Landsat imagery under the Verra VMD0006 module, cadastral parcels, regional clearing records
method: deterministic scaling identity, discrete-time hazard analysis, bootstrap confidence intervals, forward uncertainty analysis
validation: independent expanded sample of 24 cadastral parcels, directly measured activity share
measures: expanded sample mean 15.78 per cent a year against 14.99, measured activity share 0.121 against implied median 0.12
finding: Parcels cleared 14.99 per cent of their area a year, front-loaded in early years, and a scaling identity reconciled this with regional rates through an active share near 0.12.
gap_quote: Cattle ranch expansion across the Paraguayan Chaco generates parcel-level clearing rates that appear inconsistent with regional deforestation statistics, raising concerns that REDD+ baselines constructed from proxy parcels overstate forest loss (a baseline over-crediting debate that turns on denominator consistency between parcel hazard and regional flows).

title: Mapping the diversity of land uses following deforestation across Africa
area: 13.85 per cent of global forest area
data: 5 metre imagery, reference data for 15 land-use types from 30 countries
method: deep learning model trained with active learning
finding: Small-scale cropland was the dominant driver of African forest loss, with hotspots in Madagascar and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, while commodity crops dominated humid western and central Africa.
gap_quote: African forest are increasingly in decline as a result of land-use conversion due to human activities. However, a consistent and detailed characterization and mapping of land-use change that results in forest loss is not available at the spatial-temporal resolution and thematic levels suitable for decision-making at the local and regional scales

title: Seasonal Variability of Deforestation-Induced Warming in the Congo Basin Using Remote-Sensing Data
data: Global Forest Change, MODIS land surface temperature and EVI
method: linear relationship of warming to cumulative deforestation, correlation with temperature anomaly, rainfall index and EVI difference
predictors: cumulative deforestation, land surface temperature anomaly, standardised precipitation index, EVI difference from surrounding forest
finding: Warming over deforested land rose linearly with cumulative deforestation, with a typical rural complex pixel warming 0.33, 0.85 and 1.54 degrees Celsius above forest in December, January and February.
gap_quote: Deforestation impacts in the Congo Basin remain significantly understudied compared to other tropical regions.

title: Field-Based Environmental Vigilance Profiles Associated with Rural Activities in the Pool Department, Republic of the Congo
place: Republic of the Congo, Pool Department, seven localities
data: 178 field observation records
method: qualitative typology of field-recorded indicators
predictors: activity type, locality, proximity to rivers or water points, indicators affecting fragile environments and water, soil instability, potential conflicts
finding: Agriculture dominated most of seven localities, with agro-pastoral and pastoral profiles at Mindouli and Koubola and very high hydrological sensitivity at Yalavounga, Yangui and Linzolo, yielding a qualitative vigilance typology.
gap_quote: Local environmental planning requires diagnostic tools capable of identifying areas and activities that may place pressure on soils, fragile environments and water resources before these pressures become measurable deforestation or forest degradation.

title: REDD sticks and carrots in the Brazilian Amazon: Assessing costs and livelihood implications
data: historical deforestation data, enforcement mission records
method: spatially explicit model of regulatory enforcement, optimal enforcement scenario, cost and welfare analysis
validation: checked against historical deforestation and enforcement mission data
finding: Command and control was the regulator's most cost-effective REDD instrument but could cost land users over 2.5 billion reais a year for an 80 per cent deforestation cut.
gap_quote: Yet, for the large part of Amazon deforestation that occurs on non-designated public lands (terra devoluta) as well as on poorly delimited private land, PES will not be viable in the short and medium term.

title: REVISITING THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF THE CONGO STRATIFICATION MAP FOR THE YEAR 2000 USING CLOUD-BASED COMPOSITING AND OBJECT-BASED CLASSIFICATION ALGORITHMS
data: Landsat composite of nearly 2,500 scenes
method: median luminance best pixel compositing, object-based classification, area estimation by good practice
validation: stratified random sample of 1,141 reference samples
finding: A 2000 stratification map from about 2,500 Landsat scenes reached 79.32 per cent accuracy, with dense moist forest near 158.8 million hectares, 68.40 per cent of the country.
gap_quote: For the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the existing maps derived from remote sensing techniques do not allow an optimal representation of the diverse land cover classes constituting the national stratification scheme.

title: Deforestation Trends in the Congo Basin : Agriculture
data: not stated
method: IIASA modelling of agricultural sectors and trade, business-as-usual scenario
predictors: national, regional and international trends in agricultural sectors and trade
finding: Agricultural development was a key driver of deforestation in the Congo Basin, and the report set out its business-as-usual forest impacts and policy levers for forest-friendly agriculture.
gap_quote: Forest-friendly agricultural development is a challenge for the region.

title: The covariation of forest age shifts and net carbon balance over the period 2010 to 202
data: Global Age Mapping Integration v1.0 forest age dataset
method: correlation of forest age shift fractions with atmospheric inversion CO2 flux changes across eleven TRANSCOM regions
finding: Forest age fell up to 30 per cent in the Amazon, Congo Basin and Southeast Asia, 2010 to 2020, and stand replacement correlated with net CO2 release, R squared 0.37.
gap_quote: Understanding the relationship between forest age, an indicator of successional stages, and net carbon fluxes is crucial for effective forest management and climate mitigation.

title: DATA - PREDICTING LANDSCAPE DYNAMICS AND NATIVE VEGETATION LOSS IN A COASTAL ISLAND BY MEANS OF SPATIALLY EXPLICIT MODELING
data: land use and land cover maps for 2012 and 2024 reclassified into six classes
method: Dinamica EGO with Bayesian Weights of Evidence, transition probability maps, simulation
predictors: elevation, slope, soil organic carbon content, distance from urban areas, distance from rivers, distance from the coast, distance from mangrove areas, distance from roads
validation: fuzzy similarity of the 2024 simulation, windows of 3 to 11 pixels
measures: fuzzy similarity indices, value not stated
finding: Released transition probability maps, simulated land cover maps for 2013 to 2035, predictor layers and Weights of Evidence tables for a Brazilian coastal island.

title: Projet pilote REDD+ de la Lukénie
place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Bandundu province, Lukénie forest concessions
data: not stated
method: carbon stock estimation of a reference scenario, stock change calculation, monitoring protocols, financial analysis
finding: The pilot expected near 8,000 hectares of avoided deforestation and 3.5 million credits over 20 years, plus 3.6 million from reduced impact logging and 2.2 million from conservation.
gap_quote: Les principales activités du volet 1 concernent la diffusion de nouvelles pratiques agricoles, notamment agroforestières, afin de pallier les problèmes de fertilité et d'érosion des sols.

title: Sample Based Deforestation and Degradation Area Assessments for Six Central African Countries (2015-20223)
data: over 60,000 random samples visually interpreted in SEPAL and Collect Earth Online
method: sample-based area estimation from visually interpreted random samples with Open Foris tools
finding: Released spreadsheets of sample-based deforestation and degradation area estimates for six Central African countries, from over 60,000 samples visually interpreted by more than 40 experts.

title: Exploring the nexus between hydroclimatic variability, population growth, land use land cover change, and long-term upper Nyong Basin River chemistry (Central Africa rainforest)
data: Landsat 7 ETM+ and Landsat 8 OLI classification
method: supervised maximum likelihood classification, trend analysis of river chemistry
validation: accuracy assessment, reference data not stated
measures: overall accuracy 96.4 to 100 per cent, kappa 88.4 to 100 per cent
finding: Population rose from 2.6 to 4.1 million from 2005 to 2020 as 1,207 square kilometres of forest became built and farmed land, with forest falling 6.7 per cent.
gap_quote: However, there is a scientific gap on this relationship in the humid tropical zone of Central Africa.

title: Remote estimation of harvested timber volume in the Congo Basin using Sentinel-1 data
data: Sentinel-1 radar disturbance data, five near-real-time alert systems and annual change products
method: linear regression of reported harvested volume on detected disturbance area, comparison with alert and annual change products
predictors: detected disturbance area from logging gaps
validation: cross-validation, bootstrap, compared with five alert and annual change products
measures: R squared up to 0.86, bootstrap root mean square error 86,700 cubic metres, cross-validation R squared up to 0.83, rival products R squared 0.28 to 0.74
finding: Sentinel-1 logging gap area predicted reported harvest volume across 93 concessions, R squared up to 0.86, outperforming five alert and annual change products that mostly captured road corridors.
gap_quote: A third of the world’s forest area is currently used for timber production, yet independent verification of selectively logged wood volumes remains challenging.

title: Mapping the dense humid forest of Cameroon and Zaire using AVHRR satellite data
place: Cameroon, Democratic Republic of the Congo
data: NOAA AVHRR 1 kilometre data
method: classification of NOAA AVHRR data, method not named
validation: compared with Landsat MSS imagery and existing maps
finding: AVHRR data at 1 kilometre gave current maps and preliminary area estimates of dense humid forest for Cameroon and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
gap_quote: The current state of this forest is poorly known. The most recent comprehensive national forest distribution maps of the central African region are from the period between 1950-1980 and are not representative of more recent forest degradation or conversion.

title: FOREST ECOSYSTEM DYNAMICS ASSESSMENT AND PREDICTIVE MODELLING IN EASTERN HIMALAYA
place: India, Eastern Himalaya, West Bengal, Arunachal Pradesh and Assam along the Bhutan border
data: satellite imagery of 1975, 1990 and 2009
method: Cellular Automata Markov model
finding: Forest cover fell by 2,334.28 square kilometres from 1975 to 2009, at 0.35 then 0.78 per cent a year, and CA-Markov projected 4,563.34 square kilometres lost by 2028.
gap_quote: It noted progressive loss of forests in the study area between 1975 and 2009 through 1990 and predicted that, unless checked, the area is in for further depletion of the invaluable climax forests in the region, especially sal and moist deciduous forests.

title: Assessing REDD+ performance of countries with low monitoring capacities: the matrix approach
place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, one biome
data: remote sensing land cover maps
method: intact and non-intact forest stratification, transition matrix, default carbon stock change factors
finding: Proposed estimating emission trends from land cover maps through an intact and non-intact forest transition matrix with default carbon factors, tested on one Democratic Republic of the Congo biome.
gap_quote: Estimating emissions from deforestation and degradation of forests in many developing countries is so uncertain that the effects of changes in forest management could remain within error ranges (i.e. undetectable) for several years.

title: Can Logging in Equatorial Africa Affect Adjacent Parks?
data: deforestation scenario for timber concessions
method: regional-scale atmospheric simulation experiments
finding: Simulated concession deforestation cut rainfall in some adjacent parks by up to 15 per cent and raised it slightly in others, with parks downwind of clearing most sensitive.
gap_quote: Although national parks are being established to protect areas from deforestation and to conserve biodiversity, these parks are not immune to disturbances outside their boundaries.

title: Appui à la gestion durable des forêts du bassin du Congo et du bassin amazonien brésilien: Composante 3 – Action 1: développement de projets de démonstration
data: state environmental cadastre of rural properties, 2011
method: Excel model comparing returns and carbon emissions of reference and REDD+ scenarios under VCS jurisdictional guidelines, sensitivity analysis
finding: Assessed the feasibility of a municipal REDD+ programme in Mato Grosso by comparing returns and carbon emissions of reference and REDD+ scenarios, results not stated.

title: Biodiversity and Conservation Priority Setting for the Vascular Flora of New Guinea
data: forest clearance data, plant collection records
method: R-INLA spatial model of deforestation risk, joint distribution model of genera with Hmsc
predictors: cost-distance accessibility, other variables not named
validation: actual compared with predicted deforestation over 5 and 10 years, five-fold cross-validation of the biodiversity model
measures: Spearman rank correlation 0.66 over 5 years and 0.71 over 10 years, biodiversity model 0.462
finding: Relative deforestation probability predictions were accurate over 5 and 10 years, Spearman 0.66 and 0.71, and the Merauke and Jayapura lowlands combined high biodiversity with high near-term risk.
gap_quote: New Guinea is one of the world’s most floristically diverse islands, but its plant collection records are very uneven.

title: Testing methodologies for REDD+: Deforestation drivers, costs and reference levels
data: not stated
method: simple rules compared with future modelling by drivers and activities
finding: The abstract is a table fragment naming simple rules, future modelling by drivers and activities, uncertainty near plus or minus 75 per cent, and checks of national data.

title: Combined effects of climate and land‐use change on the future of humid tropical forests
place: pantropical, Amazon, Congo Basin and Asia-Oceania
data: deforestation and selective logging data
method: not stated
predictors: climate change projections, deforestation, selective logging
finding: Logging and climate change could harm biodiversity in 35 to 74 per cent of the Congo Basin, with 18 to 45 per cent of the biome left intact by 2100.
gap_quote: In the Congo, logging and climate change could negatively affect the biodiversity in 35–74% of the basin.

title: The geography of avoided deforestation and sustainable forest management offsets: the enduring question of additionality
data: pilot project databases of nearly 800 offset projects, above-ground biomass, species richness, deforestation drivers
method: Cox proportional hazards models at 50 kilometre hexagons
finding: Avoided deforestation offsets sat in areas of high biomass, species richness and stronger deforestation drivers, while over 85 per cent of forest management offsets were in the United States.
gap_quote: Avoided deforestation and sustainable forest management (AD/SFM) offset projects have developed piecemeal, lacking consensus standards and receiving only quite low carbon prices.

title: REDD+ emissions estimation and reporting: dealing with uncertainty
data: activity data and emission factors, sources not named
method: matrix approach with sensitivity analysis and Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation
finding: Fluxes varied by 4.2 to 262.2 per cent of the reference emission level, driven by fallow classification and intact forest carbon accumulation, and modelling choices caused the largest error.
gap_quote: Substantial technical challenges hinder precise and accurate estimation of forest-related emissions and removals, as well as the setting and assessment of reference levels.

title: The effect of deforestation rate on land tenure in Central Africa
data: not stated
method: conceptual analysis along the forest transition curve, theoretical land tenure model
finding: Individual land tenure increased with deforestation and continued during reforestation by plantations, suggesting tenure as an indicator of forest transition and tipping points.

title: Emissivity-based vegetation indices to monitor deforestation and forest degradation in the Congo basin rainforest
data: CAMEL combined ASTER and MODIS emissivity database
method: emissivity contrast index from infrared surface emissivity channels
finding: Proposed an emissivity contrast index from infrared surface emissivity that separates green vegetation, senescent vegetation and bare soil, unlike NDVI, using 2000 to 2016 CAMEL data.
gap_quote: Over the last decade, a severe decline in vegetation was observed in the Congo Basin rainforest, the second-largest tropical forest in the world, behind the Amazon. Therefore, actions are required to monitor and detect vegetation stresses to mitigate their negative impacts on human life, wildlife, and plant communities.

title: Random Forest Algorithm for Mapping Deforestation in the Ituri-Epulu-Aru Landscape (Democratic Republic of Congo)
place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ituri-Epulu-Aru landscape
data: optical image composites for 2003, 2010 and 2016
method: random forest classification with four sets of input variables
predictors: spectral bands nir, swir1, swir2 and red, NDVI, B54R, NDWI, NBR, elevation, slope, roughness
measures: out-of-bag error 2.15, 2.05, 1.86 and 1.85 per cent for the four models
finding: Deforestation of old-growth forest rose from 0.26 per cent a year in 2003 to 2010 to 0.66 per cent in 2010 to 2016, with 215,629 hectares lost.
gap_quote: The evaluation of deforestation by optical remote sensing remains a challenge in the humid tropical region due to high cloud cover.

title: Greenhouse gas emissions in Sub-Saharan Africa
data: FAO Tropical Forest Resources Assessment for Africa 1980 deforestation statistics, continental vegetation, soil and climate maps
method: spatially explicit land use carbon model at 9,000 points, land use strategy scenarios
finding: Modelled yearly land use carbon emissions and vegetation carbon at 9,000 points from 1985 to 2001 under forest preservation, agroforestry and plantation strategies, with other gases judged minor.

title: A multi-modal analysis of REDD+ baselines in Cambodia
data: one global and one locally calibrated forest loss dataset
method: ex-post baseline assessment methodologies with control sites, integrated across two datasets
finding: Forest loss rates varied widely with dataset and control site, and baselines of all three projects fell within or below a zone of reasonable accuracy.
gap_quote: Cambodia is facing widespread deforestation due to agriculture, logging, land grabbing, and infrastructure.

title: Quantifying selective logging impacts in Central African forests using UAV imagery: from individual trees to canopy gaps
place: Central Africa, FSC-certified selective logging sites
data: UAV imagery before and after logging, forest inventory data
method: canopy gap delineation from before and after UAV imagery, gaps linked to felled trees
predictors: species identity, tree diameter, felling conditions, forest type, topography, crown traits from allometric equations
finding: Proposed linking canopy gaps in before and after drone imagery to felled trees, relating gap size to species, diameter, felling, forest type, topography and crown traits, results not stated.
gap_quote: In Central Africa, however, region-specific data remain scarce, limiting the ability to distinguish the impacts of different logging practices and to differentiate regulatory definitions of degradation from actual ecological outcomes.

title: A full greenhouse gases budget of Africa: synthesis, uncertainties, and vulnerabilities
data: inventories, ecosystem flux measurements, models and atmospheric inversions
method: synthesis of inventories, flux measurements, models and atmospheric inversions with uncertainty quantification
finding: Africa was a small sink of 0.61 petagrams of carbon a year, central Africa the main sink, while land use change emitted 0.32, above fossil fuel emissions.
gap_quote: Uncertainties are quantified and current gaps and weaknesses in knowledge and monitoring systems described in order to guide future requirements.

title: Felids, forest and farmland: identifying high priority conservation areas in Sumatra
period: 17 years of deforestation data, years not stated
data: 17-year deforestation dataset, camera traps at 671 sites
method: occupancy modelling, cumulative resistant kernels, factorial least-cost paths, deforestation risk model not named
finding: Models predicted 1,052 square kilometres of future forest loss in the landscape, 2 to 4 per cent in core areas and 5 per cent in corridors of three threatened cats.
gap_quote: Effective planning for protected areas and wildlife population management requires a firm understanding of the location of the species’ core habitat patches, the dispersal corridors connecting them, and the risk they face from key threats, notably deforestation.

title: Natural Model based Design in Context: an Effective Method for Environmental Problems
place: Cameroon, North Cameroon, Laf Forest Reserve
data: not stated

finding: Proposed a natural language approach and the TiC tool that turn domain experts' models into simulation tools, demonstrated on deforestation of the Laf Forest Reserve in North Cameroon.
gap_quote: State-of-the-art techniques however still require both expert knowledge of the application domain and the implementation techniques as provided by ICT (such as multilevel agent technology). Domain experts, however, usually do not master ICT sufficiently.

title: Executive Summary
data: georeferenced forest cover and economic data
method: spatial prioritisation of infrastructure investments with maps of opportunity, risk and trade-offs, model not named
finding: Argues that connecting lagging and flourishing regions would boost growth, and that infrastructure siting should weigh impacts from the outset, using maps of opportunity, risk and REDD+ potential.
gap_quote: Asserts that given the vast distances and extreme variations in the spatial distribution of gross domestic product (GDP) within the Democratic Republic of Congo, connecting flourishing regions with lagging regions could provide a significant boost to economic growth, so an urgent need exists for improving both interprovincial and intraprovincial connectivity to promote trade and economic cohesion.

title: Managing Tropical Forest Ecosystems
data: not stated
method: not stated

title: Broad scale conservation: Protected areas and species interactions
place: Amazon, Congo, South American Atlantic Coast and West African forests
data: forest cover data, product not named, decadal population datasets

finding: Parks in the Amazon and Congo were large and kept high forest cover inside and around them, population growth near parks was not disproportionate, and matching gave lower protection impacts.
gap_quote: Understanding of their promise and problems is necessary to achieve conservation outcomes.

title: Monitoring Tropical Forest Degradation and Deforestation in Borneo, Southeast Asia
data: Landsat, MODIS, MERIS and SPOT VEGETATION
method: multispectral change detection, cloud-free compositing
finding: Optical change detection monitored forest change quickly but clouds limited it in the humid tropics, and Borneo fires more than tripled to about 1 million hectares in El Niño years.
gap_quote: However, the principal limitation of optical imaging systems is that they cannot penetrate clouds, which are quite frequent in the humid tropics.

title: forestatrisk: a Python package for modelling and forecasting deforestation in the tropics
data: georeferenced forest cover rasters, product not named

finding: Released forestatrisk, an open source Python package that models the spatial probability of deforestation with spatial random effects and forecasts forest cover, applied across the humid tropics to 2100.
gap_quote: The spatial random effects make possible to structure the residual spatial variability of the deforestation process, not explained by the variables of the model and often very large.

title: Mapping suitability for Buruli ulcer at fine spatial scales across Africa: A modelling study
data: deforestation and other environmental datasets, products not named

predictors: climate and atmospheric variables, damming, deforestation, other environmental variables

gap_quote: Its distribution and burden are unknown because of underdiagnosis and underreporting. It is caused by Mycobacterium ulcerans, an environmental pathogen whose environmental niche and transmission routes are not fully understood.

title: Image-based logistic regression parameters of deforestation in Rondonia, Brazil
data: Landsat classifications over 20 years
method: logistic regression

finding: Proximity to paved roads and to forest clearing edges were the strongest predictors of lot deforestation, which followed a fishbone road pattern, while suitability and soil indices explained little.

title: Expanding forest carbon sinks to mitigate climate change in Africa
data: land use change maps reclassified in ArcGIS, forest loss and gain data
method: InVEST carbon storage and sequestration model, K and S indices of forest cover change
finding: Most African countries, 77.36 per cent, lost more forest than they gained, a net 32,000 kilohectares emitting 15.73 petagrams of carbon, notably in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
gap_quote: Results indicate that deforestation , particularly in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, significantly contributes to carbon emissions, and persistent tropical deforestation will affect future greenhouse gas concentrations.

title: Mapping dry forest in Central African Republic using optical and radar data
place: Central African Republic, Sangha Mbaéré, Lobaye and Ombella-M'Poko provinces

data: not stated

finding: Direct drivers in the Congo Basin are agricultural expansion, timber extraction, infrastructure and mining, underlain by economic, technological, cultural, institutional and demographic causes, refining Geist and Lambin's framework.
gap_quote: In comparison to other rainforests around the world, the pressure on biodiversity is comparatively low in the Congo Basin. But land use intensification and climate change are poised to increase the rate of forest loss.

title: Comparing the Environmental Integrity of Emission Reductions from REDD Programs with Renewable Energy Projects
data: not stated
method: qualitative comparison of permanence, additionality, baselines, uncertainty and leakage
finding: Credits from jurisdictional REDD programmes have unique integrity strengths, renewable energy credits have their own weaknesses, and REDD has faced scrutiny other sectors escaped.
gap_quote: However, various publications have questioned whether carbon credits from REDD should be accepted under market-based mechanisms, and have identified issues regarding their environmental integrity and their ability to offset emissions from other sectors.

title: Valuation of forest carbon stocks to estimate the potential for result-based payment under REDD+ in Cameroon
data: values from existing literature

gap_quote: The current study thus provides basic information which can help to enrich the debate on the feasibility of REDD+ implementation in Cameroon.

title: A global assessment of closed forests, deforestation and malaria risk

title: Review and combination of recent remote sensing based products for forest cover change assessments in Cameroon

finding: Deforestation intensity fell from the 1990s to the 2000s, Cameroon's loss peaked near the Atlantic coast with much outside the forest domain, and Landsat missed degradation.
gap_quote: The Landsat spatial resolution used in the two products allows us to capture change caused by agro-industrial exploitation as well as shifting cultivation, infrastructure and selective logging when the area affected is large enough. But it fails to monitor forest degradation and small scale deforestation events.

title: Reading the logging scars in Congo Basin forest cover
data: not stated
method: not stated
finding: Selective logging dominates the Congo Basin, sustainable harvest intensity depends on ecosystem resilience, and forest recovery after deforestation and degradation is slower on sandy, resource-poor soils.

title: The Climate and Land-Use Change Feedback in the Congo Basin
data: not stated
method: synthesis of observational evidence and climate model scenarios
finding: Continued forest loss could turn the Congo Basin into a carbon source, and scenarios show deforestation cutting rainfall up to 10 per cent and warming about 0.7 degrees by 2050.
gap_quote: The Congo Basin, home to the world’s second-largest tropical rainforest, plays a pivotal role in regulating global climate through carbon sequestration, rainfall recycling, and temperature regulation. However, the acceleration of the land-use changes—driven by agriculture, logging, mining, and urbanization—is eroding these vital ecosystem services.

title: Remote Sensing for the Audit and Assurance of the Carbon Market

method: not stated

title: Analyse de l’évolution des paramètres climatiques et des pressions sur les ressources forestières au Nord d’Idiofa dans la province du Kwilu en République Démocratique du Congo

gap_quote: Les ressources forestières mondiales subissent des pressions dues aux activités humaines, et la forêt recule de 13 millions d’hectares par année surtout dans la zone intertropicale.

title: A Comparative Study of Deep Learning and CA-Markov Methods for Land Use / Land Cover Change Prediction
data: Sentinel-1A images

gap_quote: The analysis of LULCC is a real challenge and can be very useful in various fields.

title: Institutional analysis of causes of deforestation in REDD+ pilot sites in the Equateur province: Implication for REDD+ in the Democratic Republic of Congo
place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Equateur province, two REDD+ pilot sites
data: not stated

gap_quote: As DRC moves from REDD+ readiness to implementation, analysis of the causes of deforestation at the local level is paramount.

title: Analysis of the Impact of Land-Use/Land-Cover Change on Land-Surface Temperature in the Villages within the Luki Biosphere Reserve

data: remote sensing imagery, land surface temperature

gap_quote: Consequently, examining the variation of land-surface temperatures and mitigating the related impacts remain a challenge.

title: Forest extent monitoring in the Congo Basin using L-band Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR)

title: Towards the use of satellite-based tropical forest disturbance alerts to assess selective logging intensities
data: RADD alerts, PlanetScope monthly mosaics

title: Should We Include Avoidance of Deforestation in the International Response to Climate Change?
data: FAO deforestation estimates, IPCC emission estimates
method: not stated

gap_quote: Global deforestation and forest degradation rates have a significant impact on the accumulation of greenhouse gases (GHG) in the atmosphere.

title: Modelling land-atmosphere interactions in tropical Africa: the climatic impact of deforestation in the Congo basin
place: Congo Basin, tropical Africa, Kisangani in the Democratic Republic of the Congo

gap_quote: The demand foragricultural land in the Congo basin is expected to yield substantialdeforestation over the coming decades.

title: Contribution of artisanal chainsaw milling to forest degradation in Central Africa
place: Cameroon, Democratic Republic of the Congo
data: field visits to 120 chainsaw milling sites

finding: Of trees felled at 120 chainsaw milling sites in Cameroon and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, 84 per cent stood in undisturbed forest near degraded zones.
gap_quote: Various interventions to regulate and professionalise chainsaw milling are needed to support the diversity of their production strategies, but two measures seem essential: formal chainsaw milling permits need to be made available at lower cost and the range of timber species on the national markets should be expanded, especially in DRC.

title: Deforestation in Tahura Sekitar Tanjung Province Jambi
place: Indonesia, Jambi Province, Tahura Sekitar Tanjung
data: not stated

gap_quote: Deforestation cause damage to the environment, climate change and greenhouse gas emissions.

title: Key Factors Driving Deforestation in North-Kivu Province, Eastern DR-Congo Using GIS and Remote Sensing

gap_quote: Deforestation has become one of major problems in tropical forest regions.

title: Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Land Use Change and Prediction in an Artisanal Mining Hotspot: A Multi-Decadal Study of the Kampene Mining Area, DRC

Despite their socio-economic importance, mining activities cause significant alterations to the environment, especially due to their impact on forest cover.

title: Analysing land use/land cover change and prediction in a cloudy urban area using SAR: the case of Douala, Cameroon
data: SAR imagery in several polarisations

gap_quote: Land use/land cover change analyses and prediction remains a fundamental tool in shaping urban decision making.

title: Greenhouse gas emissions and their trends over the last 3 decades across Africa

gap_quote: The main source of uncertainty comes from CO2 fluxes in the LULUCF sector, for which the spread across inversions is larger than 50 %, especially in central Africa.

title: TINGKAT RUJUKAN EMISI HUTAN MANGROVE DELTA MAHAKAM
data: not stated

gap_quote: Over the observation period of 1980-2001, conversion of mangrove forest into aquaculture ponds has resulted in a massive mangrove loss, with an estimation of 3,183 hectare/year, or equivalent to the release of 0.46 Tg CO2e/year.

title: Modeling unplanned landscape change: A Colombian case study
place: Colombia, Caquetá colonisation front, Colombian Amazon

gap_quote: Land cover change is an important global issue because of the expanding ecological footprint of a rapidly increasing human population and per capita level of resource consumption.

title: CHARACTERIZING HYDROLOGICAL PROCESSES WITHIN THE DATA-SCARCE ENVIRONMENT OF THE CONGO BASIN
place: Congo Basin, Democratic Republic of the Congo

gap_quote: The Congo Basin’s streams and rivers could be impacted by human activities in the region, notably by land cover and land use change (LCLUC) considering the strong interactions between hydrology and ecosystem processes in the humid tropics.

title: Investigating the impact of a long-term research and conservation project on the expansion of land use and land cover in a remote area of central DRC
place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Mai-Ndombe Province, Salonga National Park buffer zone, LuiKotale

gap_quote: Deforestation due to logging, mining, and burning are of particular severity in tropical rainforests with the Amazonian and Congolese basins harboring the largest reminders on our planet.

title: Patterns of (future) environmental risks from cocoa expansion and intensification in West Africa call for context specific responses
place: West African cocoa zone, Ghana, Côte d'Ivoire, Liberia, Cameroon
data: past deforestation trends, cocoa climatic suitability

finding: Cocoa expansion threatens ecologically important West African areas in varied patterns compounded by climate change, needing protection and restoration in Ghana and Côte d'Ivoire and planning in Cameroon.
gap_quote: Cocoa is an important historical driver and direct cause of forest loss and degradation in the West African Upper Guinean biodiversity hotspot.

title: Regional feedbacks among fire, climate, and tropical deforestation
place: Amazon, Congo, Indonesia and New Guinea

method: NCAR CCM3.2 general circulation model, McArthur forest fire danger index, fire occurrence related to the index

finding: Deforestation raised fire danger 41, 56 and 58 per cent and fire frequency 44, 80 and 123 per cent in the Amazon, Congo and Indonesia, mainly through wind and drying.
gap_quote: Using the observed relationship between FFDI and fire occurrence, we estimate increases in fire frequency of 44, 80, and 123%, in the Amazon, Congo, and Indonesia, respectively, with deforestation.

title: Vertical Canopy structure and Very high-resolution Remote Sensing tools for forest Degradation monitoring in the Congo Basin
place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Yangambi, Congo Basin

finding: Industrial logging increased canopy gaps in mixed forests but not in Gilbertiodendron stands or under artisanal logging, and a 500 dollar drone matched LiDAR gap area at one hectare.
gap_quote: Unlike deforestation, forest degradation monitoring remains constrained by the lack of a consensual definition and operational indicators, particularly in the Congo Basin.

title: Roads, Forests, and the Biodiversity of the Democratic Republic of Congo

title: Assessment of Spatial Dynamics of Forest Cover in Lomami National Park (DR Congo), 2008–2024: Implications for Conservation and Sustainable Ecosystem Management

title: Humid tropical forest monitoring with multi-temporal L-, C- and X-band SAR data

title: Mapping tropical coastal vegetation using JERS-1 and ERS-1 radar data with a decision tree classifier

title: ASSESSMENT OF LAND USE/LAND COVER CHANGE MAPPING IN BANGUI CITY USING REMOTE SENSING AND GIS TECHNIQUES

title: Salience, credibility and legitimacy in land use change modeling : model validation as product or process?

title: The forgotten D: challenges of addressing forest degradation in complex mosaic landscapes under REDD+

title: The Mangrove Forests of the Cameroon Coast and its Socio-Economic Significan

title: A Generalized Deforestation and Land-Use Change Scenario Generator for Use in Climate Modelling Studies

title: Could IFM REDD+ projects incentivize forest concessionaires to reduce greenhouse gases emissions in Central Africa? A lesson from the FORAFAMA project. [P-3331-01]

title: Gorillas in the midst: the impact of armed conflict on the conservation of protected areas in sub-Saharan Africa

title: Congo Basin Forests: Description

title: Reliably mapping low-intensity forest disturbance using satellite radar data

data: Sentinel-1 VV GRD time series, UAV LiDAR, terrestrial laser scanning and field inventory reference, Global Forest Watch Tree Cover Loss, RADD alerts
method: Cumulative Sum change detection on Sentinel-1 time series, regression of biomass change on the change metric
validation: UAV LiDAR reference map, compared with Global Forest Watch Tree Cover Loss and RADD alerts
measures: success rate 78 per cent in Gabon and 65 per cent in Peru, R2 0.95 with AGB change, R2 0.83 with canopy height loss, 61 per cent overlap with Global Forest Watch
finding: CuSum on Sentinel-1 found disturbances down to 0.01 ha with 78 per cent success in Gabon and 65 per cent in Peru, and GFW and RADD largely missed low-intensity ones.
gap_quote: Despite recent advances, mapping subtle forest losses, such as those due to small-scale and irregular selective logging, remains problematic.

title: Large-scale estimation of forest canopy opening using remote sensing in Central Africa
place: Central Africa, where the Central African Republic, Republic of the Congo and Cameroon meet
period: thirty years of Landsat archives, years not stated
data: Landsat image archives, continental land cover maps
method: semi-automatic Landsat processing chain with a canopy opening index calibrated to a low-resolution radiometer
finding: A semi-automatic Landsat chain estimated present and past canopy opening, a measure of degradation, over thirty years where the Central African Republic, Republic of the Congo and Cameroon meet.
gap_quote: Capacities for measuring the extent of the damage are essential to the calculation of carbon emissions under REDD+ programmes (Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation).

title: From conceptual model to implementation model Piloting a multi-level case study in Cameroon.
data: not stated

title: Application de Télédétection et des SIG dans la cartographie de l'érosion côtière à Cap Cameroun
place: Cameroon, Cape Cameroon in the Wouri estuary near Douala
data: Landsat classification for 1975, 1986, 2000 and 2018

finding: From 1986 to 2014, Cape Cameroon lost more than 103 ha of land to coastal erosion, and mangroves degraded at a rate of 13.68 per cent.
gap_quote: Coastal erosion is very intense and affects populations and ecosystems.

title: Modeling the Conversion of Forest Land to Other Types of Occupation Due to Urban Growth in Five Forest Towns in the Congo Basin
place: Republic of the Congo, Ouesso, Pokola, Ngombe, Impfondo and Dongou
data: land cover maps for 1986, 2003 and 2019
method: explanatory model of forest loss, not named, with forecasts to 2050
predictors: shifting agriculture, wood fuel collection, construction wood collection, illegal logging, urban expansion, population growth
finding: Shifting agriculture was 48 per cent of direct causes of deforestation around five towns, and forest loss is forecast to increase by 487.20 to 5266.73 ha by 2050.
gap_quote: Understanding the direct and indirect factors of these conversions from local studies in the tropics is essential to project the future impact of human activities on the preservation of tropical forests in general and the forests of the Republic of Congo in particular.

title: Towards Land Use Dynamics Modeling: A Case Study of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
data: land cover classes, product not named
method: constrained regression weighted areal interpolation, network analysis with friction surfaces
predictors: population density, accessibility, protected areas, forest concessions
validation: predicted population compared with observed population by Territory
finding: Regression weighted areal interpolation mapped population density by land cover class at 1 km, and network analysis with friction surfaces gave a realistic national accessibility measure.
gap_quote: Unfortunately, central African countries, as the DRC, often lack reliable and detailed census data.

title: A review of spatial models of forest regeneration to guide forest restoration in Latin America.
data: not stated
method: not stated
finding: Spatial models of forest regeneration in Latin America, adapted from deforestation frameworks, simulated regeneration inaccurately, and a framework with finer resolution, stratification and two-way gain and loss modelling is proposed.
gap_quote: Modelling frameworks originally designed for tropical deforestation or similarly abrupt land change have become widely adopted, but are poorly suited to capture the relatively progressive and nuanced dynamics of forest regeneration.

title: Land Use and Land Cover changes in the Centre Region of Cameroon.
data: Landsat TM and OLI classification, MAPBOX high resolution images, 1951 aerial photograph, SPOT 6 image of 2006
method: maximum likelihood classification, Markov model projection in IDRISI Selva
finding: Centre Region forest fell 54 per cent in thirty years, and a Markov projection showed dense forest falling from 45 per cent in 2015 to 0.25 per cent by 2050.
gap_quote: It was estimated that by 2050, the entire dense forest can be depleted if nothing is done, while only 12.67% of the secondary forest would remain in the Region.

title: Spatial Dimensions of Existing Conservation Areas and Other Land Uses in the Congo Basin
place: Congo Basin, with Gabon, Democratic Republic of the Congo and Cameroon named
data: not stated
method: not stated
finding: Remote sensing and machine learning improve forest and conservation area mapping, though some Congo Basin maps lack government validation, and mapping and spatial data policies would aid planning.
gap_quote: Adopting innovative policies on mapping (Indonesia’s one map policy, Rwanda National land registry) and spatial data management (Geoportal for the Region, The INSPIRE Directive) will be very helpful in planning and conserving the Congo Basin.

title: Multi-Temporal and Multi-Frequency SAR Analysis for Forest Land Cover Mapping of the Mai-Ndombe District (Democratic Republic of Congo)
place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Mai-Ndombe District
data: Sentinel-1 C-band and ALOS-2 PALSAR-2 L-band SAR, Global Forest Change and JAXA ALOS forest and non-forest maps
method: multivariate maximum likelihood supervised classification of multi-temporal SAR backscatter statistics
validation: systematic sampling grid of manual interpretations of very high resolution optical images, compared with Global Forest Change and JAXA forest and non-forest maps
measures: overall accuracy 84.4, 89.1 and 90.0 per cent for C-band, L-band and combined three-class maps, 90.3, 92.2 and 93.3 per cent for forest and non-forest maps
finding: Combined C and L band SAR mapped best, with overall accuracy of 90.0 per cent for three classes and 93.3 per cent for forest and non-forest.
gap_quote: We investigate whether and to what extent the denser time series of C- band SAR can compensate for the L-band’s deeper vegetation penetration depth and known better FLC mapping performance.

title: Dynamiques d'urbanisation et risques écosystemiques dans la région de Libreville (Gabon)
data: remote sensing land use classification, imagery not named
method: remote sensing and GIS land use and risk mapping, prospective land use simulation under laissez-faire and control scenarios, semi-structured interviews
finding: Libreville grew fast with heavy deforestation, mainly to the north, and simulation showed dense vegetation in protected areas falling sharply under laissez-faire but almost fully kept under a control scheme.
gap_quote: Des questions peu abordées au Gabon sont soulevées : comment, par qui et pourquoi l'urbanisation anarchique est-elle produite ?

title: A stepwise framework for developing REDD+ reference levels
data: not stated
method: not stated
finding: Reference levels should follow a stepwise approach, with methods set by data availability and quality and adjusted for drivers, to suit country capacities and allow improvement over time.
gap_quote: Developing forest reference (emission) levels for REDD+ is an urgent and challenging task, given the lack of quality data in many countries, genuine uncertainties about future rates of deforestation and forest degradation and potential incentives for biasing the estimates.

title: Different contexts, same concerns? Wood gap and forest restoration in Indonesia and Cameroon
period: 1982 to 2016 for Indonesia, not stated for Cameroon
data: not stated
method: comparative case analysis of two countries
finding: Both countries filled wood gaps through illegal practices, low wood prices deterred restoration, and Cameroon's deforestation was 0.2 per cent a year but rapid near cities and roads.
gap_quote: In Cameroon, the growing demand for timber is accelerated by domestic market paired with the population growth above 2.5% per year. Domestic timber and firewood are sourced from poorly managed non-permanent and permanent forest. The rate of deforestation at the national level remains low (0.2 % per year), but deforestation is rapid around cities and along roads.

title: Forecasting deforestation and carbon emissions in tropical developing countries facing demographic expansion: a case study in M adagascar
place: Madagascar, five study areas in humid and spiny-dry forest
period: data years not stated, projected to 2030
data: not stated

gap_quote: To plan efficient climate change mitigation programs (such as REDD+, Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and forest Degradation), reliable forecasts of deforestation and carbon dioxide emissions are necessary.

title: Estimation par régression de l'incertitude des cartes de pertes de couvert forestier au Cameroun
data: national forest extent and loss map of Cameroon for 2000 to 2015, SPOT 6, Sentinel-2 and Landsat 7 and 8 images for reference
method: regression estimator, stratified random sampling combined with a model-assisted approach on 1 km segments, confusion matrix
validation: independent reference sample of 348 points and 1000 segments of 1 km, visually interpreted apart from the map producers
measures: 64 of 118 deforestation reference samples undetected, omission of forest loss 54 per cent
finding: The national forest loss map missed 54 per cent of forest loss in the emission reduction programme area, mainly in cropland, and overestimated forest.
gap_quote: L'étude propose une méthode statistique robuste pour réduire les incertitudes des cartes forestières existantes de 2000 à 2015 au Cameroun.

title: National forest cover change in Congo Basin: deforestation, reforestation, degradation and regeneration for the years 1990, 2000 and 2005.
place: Congo Basin, six Central African countries with tropical moist forest
data: high resolution imagery at 547 systematic sample sites
method: object-based automatic classification with national expert interpretation on a systematic sample
predictors: population density, small-scale agriculture, fuelwood collection, forest accessibility, timber extraction, protected areas
measures: 92.7 per cent agreement of tree cover classes
finding: Annual net deforestation in the Congo Basin was 0.09 per cent for 1990 to 2000 and 0.17 per cent for 2000 to 2005, and net degradation 0.05 and 0.09.

title: An assessment of recent peat forest disturbances and their drivers in the Cuvette Centrale, Africa
place: Cuvette Centrale, Republic of the Congo and Democratic Republic of the Congo
data: peatland maps, Radar for Detecting Deforestation alerts, monthly Planet and Sentinel-2A images
method: spatial and temporal hotspot analysis of alerts, visual interpretation of 2267 random samples for direct drivers
predictors: direct driver class, distance to peat forest edge, distance to roads and rivers, forest concessions, protected areas
finding: From 2019 to 2021, 91 per cent of Cuvette Centrale peat forest disturbance was in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and smallholder agriculture caused over 88 per cent.
gap_quote: The largest tropical peatland complex in the Cuvette Centrale is marked by persistent knowledge gaps.

title: Time-series maps of aboveground carbon stocks in the forests of central Sumatra
place: Indonesia, Riau province of central Sumatra
period: data years not stated, projected to 2030
data: radar and LiDAR with field measurements of carbon stocks
method: radar and LiDAR carbon stock mapping, spatially explicit modelling of carbon stock change under business as usual, conservation and concession scenarios
measures: accuracy plus or minus 23.5 Mg C per ha
finding: Riau's natural forests stored 265 million Mg C, and under business as usual carbon stocks could fall 75 per cent by 2030, releasing 747 million Mg CO2.
gap_quote: Efforts to reduce emissions from deforestation and forest degradation in tropical Asia require accurate high-resolution mapping of forest carbon stocks and predictions of their likely future variation.

title: Landscape change in the bamenda highlands of Northwestern Cameroon: Modeling the driving forces of smallholder deforestation
place: Cameroon, Bamenda highlands, Kilum-Ijim mountain forest and watersheds
data: satellite imagery, sensor not named
method: remote sensing change trajectory analysis, spatial explanatory model of land cover change, type not named
predictors: biophysical variables, locational context, household socioeconomic factors, proximity to road, land suitability
finding: Over 1978 to 2008, land cover change around the Kilum-Ijim forest raised crops and cattle but risked biodiversity loss, and was explained by variables including road proximity and land suitability.
gap_quote: Overall, the documented land cover changes increase provisioning services such as crops and cattle that are characteristic some of the cultural landscapes in the area but may cause an irreversible loss of biodiversity and a depletion of other ecological services provided by forests and shrublands.

title: Allocating the REDD+ national baseline to local projects: A case study of Cambodia
data: forest area and forest carbon stock change, source not named
method: Partitioning Around Medoids cluster analysis of 127 districts, four baseline allocation methods weighted by deforestation risk
finding: Allocation by historical forest carbon stock change fitted the reference period idea best, while snapshot methods gave more baseline to high-forest projects regardless of deforestation trend.
gap_quote: These differences suggest that the ‘snapshot’ methods do not consider the inequity in the amount of baseline allocated to the projects.

title: Using models to inform policies to meet multiple objectives. Sustainable development, climate change mitigation and biodiversity conservation in Central Africa
place: Central Africa, member countries of the Central Africa Forest Commission
data: not stated
method: land use change model projections under macro-economic and land use policy scenarios
finding: Land use projections for Central Africa showed effective protected areas and concessions conserve great apes with negligible cost to agricultural production, and more protected area could reduce species habitat loss.
gap_quote: Member countries of the Central Africa Forest Commission (COMIFAC) have committed to sustainable management of the region’s forests, including under the COMIFAC “Convergence Plan”, and to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Achieving these objectives is dependent on the development, and implementation, of new and existing national policies and approaches.

title: Stimulating Implementation of Sustainable Development Goals and Conservation Action: Predicting Future Land Use/Cover Change in Virunga National Park, Congo
place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Virunga National Park
data: satellite image classification for 2010, 2015 and 2019, sensor not named
method: cross-tabulation change analysis, transition potentials by machine learning, Markov chain change prediction
predictors: accessibility, landscape topography, proximity to existing human activities
finding: A Markov chain and machine learning simulation projected agricultural expansion and urban development reducing Virunga's forest and open land by 2030, driven by accessibility and proximity to human activity.
gap_quote: However, population growth, increased urbanisation, deforestation, and rapid economic development has decidedly modified the surface of the earth, resulting in dramatic land cover changes, which continue to cause significant degradation of environmental attributes.

title: Wilderness conservation in the Anthropocene
place: global, with Central Africa, the Amazon and Niassa National Reserve in Mozambique named
data: global human pressure dataset at 1 km2 for 1993 to 2009, forest loss data not named
method: spatial analysis of wilderness change, spatial framework of threat and species co-occurrence, assessment of protected site condition
finding: Global wilderness fell by 3.3 million km2 from 1993 to 2009, with the greatest losses in the Amazon and Central Africa, and human impacts covered 84 per cent of land.
gap_quote: A spatial analysis of changes in wilderness extentbetween 1993 and 2009 showed catastrophic declines amounting to 3.3 million km2, withthe greatest losses occurring in the Amazon and Central Africa (appendix 2).

title: Reducing Deforestation and Trading Emissions: Economic Implications for the Post-Kyoto Carbon Market
data: not stated
method: numerical equilibrium model of the global carbon market linked with a dynamic partial equilibrium model of the forestry sector, uncertainty analysis of transaction costs and baselines
finding: Crediting avoided deforestation in emissions trading by 2020 would lower post-Kyoto policy costs and bring tropical regions large revenues, with transaction costs and baselines driving uncertainty.
gap_quote: Regarding uncertainties of this future carbon abatement option, we find both forestry transaction costs and deforestation baselines to play an important role for the post-Kyoto carbon market.

title: Modelling land use changes in the Republic of Congo 2000-2030. A report by the REDD-PAC project. Short report
place: Republic of the Congo in the title, Democratic Republic of the Congo in the abstract
data: not stated
method: land use change modelling, model not named
finding: The short report modelled land use change to identify areas under greatest future conversion pressure and their consequences for agricultural production, greenhouse gas emissions and biodiversity, with no results given.

title: Modelling forest degradation and risk of disease outbreaks in mainland Equatorial Guinea
data: open data on deforestation, product not named
method: composite index of emerging infectious disease risk combining exposure and vulnerability, ecotone modelling, accessibility modelling, zonal statistics
predictors: proximity to deforested areas, proximity to ecotones, travel time to hospitals
finding: In mainland Equatorial Guinea, all people lived within 15 minutes of hazardous areas, and 10.7 per cent faced medium or high emerging infectious disease risk.
gap_quote: Epidemiologists have testified for a rise of emerging infectious diseases (EID) events in the tropical areas undergoing forest clearance episodes and make the case for their association to forest degradation and loss.

title: Endogenous Targeting and the Additionality of Conservation
data: not stated
method: staggered difference-in-differences with matching on deforestation risk predicted by a Random Survival Forest
predictors: protected area status, predicted deforestation risk
finding: Bolivian protected areas reduced deforestation by 0.19 percentage points on average, with no effect in low-risk areas, where they were overrepresented, and up to 0.50 in high-risk areas.
gap_quote: The world has lost one-third of its forests, with those in the tropics facing the most rapid decline despite their substantial ecological and climate benefits. Protected areas (PAs) have become the primary policy instrument to curb deforestation, yet they are often established where deforestation pressure is relatively low and potential conservation gains are limited.

title: Understanding the mechanism of land-cover related climate change in the low latitudes
place: Africa, with the Congo Basin and sub-Saharan West Africa named
data: idealized vegetation reduction scenarios
method: sensitivity experiments with a synoptic-scale regional climate model
finding: Removing African vegetation in a regional climate model reduced seasonal rainfall, most over the Congo Basin and West Africa, by up to 2000 and 600 mm, through lower evapotranspiration.
gap_quote: Understanding the local and dynamical effects of land-cover changes is crucial to future climate prediction, given ongoing population growth and increasing agricultural needs in Africa.

title: Detecting and prediting changes in mangrove forest in West and Central Africa using Landsat satellite data
data: Landsat classification
method: supervised classification, change detection, Probabilistic Landscape Modelling and Simulation Tool
finding: Mangrove in West and Central Africa fell about 16.9 per cent from 1988 to 2014 with 2.5 per cent recovered, and was projected unchanged or slightly lower to 2027.
gap_quote: At the same time, mangrove in many parts of the world are declining at an alarming rate-possibly.

title: Driving forces of tropical deforestation: The role of remote sensing and spatial models
data: satellite image classification, sensor not named
method: brief review of spatial methods, satellite image classification, change analysis, econometric modelling
finding: Image classification, change analysis and econometric modelling identified deforestation rates, hotspots and the relative roles of biophysical and socioeconomic drivers in the southern Yucatán, with no values given.

title: Linking forests, deforestation, and nutritional outcomes: an observational study in nine African countries
place: Africa, nine countries including Cameroon and the Democratic Republic of the Congo
data: spatially explicit forest cover and loss data, product not named
method: generalised linear mixed-effects models
predictors: forest cover and loss within 10 km of communities, climate, infrastructure, economy, demography
finding: Children near more forest had 10.8 per cent lower underweight incidence in urban areas but 6.0 per cent higher in rural areas, and deforestation was linked to more underweight.
gap_quote: Agricultural expansion is a leading driver of deforestation, yet malnutrition remains a significant cause of morbidity.

title: Projecting Global Changes in Land Use and Ecosystem Services Using SEALS (Spatial Economic Allocation Landscape Simulator)
data: coarse land use change projections for six Shared Socioeconomic Pathway scenarios, base map not named

validation: compared with conventional estimates from low-resolution inputs and with prior estimates
finding: SEALS downscaled six SSP scenarios to 300 m, projecting 3 to 21 per cent less carbon storage by 2100, largest under SSPs 3 and 4 with heavy tropical deforestation.
gap_quote: Understanding how economic systems and ecosystems interact across space is crucial to ensure societal needs are met without compromising environmental quality.

title: Assessment of land use and land cover (LULC) and vegetation degradation state from wildfire within the scope of forest landscape restoration (FLR) in Cameroon
place: Cameroon, forest and savannah transition zone
data: Landsat 7 and 8 images for 2001, 2015 and 2023
method: random forest classification in Google Earth Engine with spectral indices, burned area and fire frequency analysis by land cover class
predictors: land use and land cover class, vegetation cover, conservation zone status
measures: accuracy 83 to 96 per cent, F1-score, precision and recall values not stated
finding: Random forest maps of 2001 to 2023 showed dense forest falling 6.9 per cent, and savannah and farmland were most burned, at 30 to 36 per cent, and most degraded.
gap_quote: Forest-Savannah transition zones are increasingly vulnerable due to their position between the savannah and forest ecosystems, and their ecological and biophysical characteristics.

title: Changes in the area of optimal tree cover of a declining Afro‐Palaearctic migrant across the species’ wintering range
place: sub-Saharan Africa wintering range, surveys in four West African countries, Democratic Republic of the Congo named
data: satellite remote sensing tree cover data for 2000 to 2014, product not named
method: occurrence of Wood Warbler modelled against tree cover from survey data, extrapolated across the wintering range
finding: Optimal tree cover of 40 to 61 per cent for Wood Warblers grew 46.7 per cent from 2000 to 2014, as 27,683 km2 of closed forest degraded into that range.
gap_quote: Land use change in sub‐Saharan Africa continues apace, but its role in driving the declines of Afro‐Palaearctic migrant birds is unknown. This is due partly to a lack of knowledge of migrants’ requirements on the wintering grounds, and of spatially explicit assessments of land cover change.

title: Deforestation Effects on Soil Erosion in the Lake Kivu Basin, D.R. Congo-Rwanda
place: Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda, Lake Kivu basin
data: land cover and land use for 2015, source not named
method: Universal Soil Erosion Equation model, with conservation practice scenarios
predictors: land use and land cover, precipitation, slope, conservation practice
finding: Lake Kivu basin soil loss averaged 30 t per ha a year, and cropland, on 74 per cent of the land, produced 75 per cent of it.
gap_quote: Deforestation and natural grassland conversion to agricultural land use constitute a major threat to soil and water conservation.

title: Anthropisation et dynamique spatio-tamporelle de paysages forestiers en République démocratique du Congo
data: land cover dynamics, imagery not named
method: landscape ecology indices of structure and composition, spatio-temporal land cover change analysis, correlation with human factors
predictors: proximity to cities, city socioeconomic importance, population density, tracks and roads opened by logging companies
finding: Human activity drove forest landscape change in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with degradation and loss correlated with nearness to cities and population density, and access following logging roads.
gap_quote: A l’image du bassin du Congo, la République Démocratique du Congo (République Démocratique du Congo) fait face à une réduction de la qualité et de la superficie de son couvert forestier.

title: Multi-Temporal Landsat Remote Sensing for Forest Landscape Fragmentation Analysis in the Yoko Forest, Kisangani, DRC
place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Yoko Forest Reserve near Kisangani
data: Landsat classification
method: unsupervised classification in ENVI, supervised classification in ArcGIS 10, fragmentation analysis
finding: Landsat classification showed large-scale human-induced fragmentation of the Yoko forest landscape from 1976 to 2015, with no rates given.
gap_quote: If these trends continue, they will affect the sustainability of water resources and livelihoods in the Congo Basin of the Democratic Republic of Congo.

title: MAPPING DEFORESTATION IN THE CONGO BASIN FOREST USING MULTI-TEMPORAL SPOT-VGT IMAGERY FROM 2000 TO 2004
place: Central Africa, 15 degrees south to 15 degrees north and 5 to 35 degrees east
