finding: Annual SPOT-VEGETATION NDVI composites gave new vegetation maps for Central Africa and an RGB-NDVI change detection of biomass loss and gain for 2000 to 2004, with no figures given.
gap_quote: The NDVI analysis will- in the near future- be applied to study reflectance behaviour in single channels to obtain a better accuracy for our classification results.

title: Spatiotemporal Dynamics of Land Use and Land Cover Change in the Ebo Forest Reserve, Littoral Region of Cameroon
place: Cameroon, Ebo Forest Reserve, Littoral Region
data: Landsat classification
method: supervised classification
measures: overall accuracy 99.08 per cent in 1994, 99.89 per cent in 2009 and 100 per cent in 2024
finding: Ebo Forest Reserve dense forest fell from 98.0 to 82.0 per cent from 1994 to 2024, while settlements and bare soil rose from 0.2 to 9.7 per cent.
gap_quote: The findings underscore the need for a balanced approach to managing LULC changes and climate impacts, ensuring sustainable resource management while supporting community development.

title: Impacts of Land Use/Land Cover Change and Climate Change on Natural Hazards in Tropical Regions: Synthesis Review and Relevance to the Kinshasa (DRC) Context
place: tropical regions, with Kinshasa in the Democratic Republic of the Congo
data: not stated
method: thematic narrative review of 144 references
finding: Urbanization, deforestation and climate variability combine to worsen flooding, erosion, landslides and heat in tropical cities such as Kinshasa, so integrated spatially explicit risk assessments are needed.
gap_quote: In Kinshasa, these effects are amplified by fragile soils, steep topography, and rapid, unplanned urban growth.

title: THE IMPACT OF DEFORESTATION ON BIODIVERSITY LOSS: A STUDY ON THE EFFECTS OF HABITAT DESTRUCTION IN TROPICAL RAINFORESTS
place: pantropical, Amazon, Congo Basin and Southeast Asia, 15 countries
data: Landsat, MODIS and Sentinel images, field biodiversity surveys at 350 sites
method: problem-based synthesis of remote sensing, field surveys and ecological modelling, fragment size analysis, species-area relationships
predictors: commercial agriculture, logging, small-scale agriculture, infrastructure
finding: Deforestation rose 42 per cent since 2000, removing 1.5 million km2, commercial agriculture caused 65 per cent, and 15 to 37 per cent of species could face extinction by 2050.
gap_quote: Carbon emissions from tropical deforestation represent 8-10% of annual global anthropogenic emissions, with primary forest loss releasing 30% more carbon than previously estimated due to unaccounted below-ground biomass.

title: Landslide risk trends in the Kivu Rift and the impact of environmental and societal dynamics
place: Kivu Rift, Burundi, eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda
data: 1958 forest cover from about 2,400 aerial photographs, satellite forest cover products for 1988, 2001 and 2016, landslide and deforestation data for 2000 to 2016
method: cellular automaton reconstruction of annual forest cover, contemporary deforestation and landslide relationship applied to past forest change, risk as hazard times population density
finding: Kivu Rift landslide risk was higher in the Democratic Republic of the Congo than in Rwanda and Burundi, rising in the 1990s with displacement onto steep land and deforestation.
gap_quote: Although the link between deforestation and landslide hazard/risk has been widely recognized, it remains poorly quantified. This is especially the case in the Global South where historical land cover and landslide records are scarce.

title: Exploitation des algorithmes d'apprentissage profond et des séries temporelles d'images satellitaires pour la prédiction de la déforestation
data: Sentinel-1 image time series
method: deep learning, three architectures compared, hybrid CNN-LSTM prediction model named Deforest_Pred, compared with CA-Markov
finding: The thesis built a Sentinel-1 workflow, compared three deep learning architectures, validated them against CA-Markov and proposed a hybrid CNN-LSTM deforestation prediction model for the Dja Biosphere Reserve.

title: Dynamics of Land Use and Land Cover Change in the South Talihya Watershed North Kivu, Eastern Democratic Republic of Congo
place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, South Talihya watershed, North Kivu
data: Landsat TM images of 1987 and 2001, Sentinel-2 image of 2020
method: diachronic image classification, classifier not named

gap_quote: The anthropization of forest ecosystems has become a major environmental problem with negative impacts on biodiversity around the world. Responding to such a problem requires monitoring land use.

title: On the potential for strategic behavior in jurisdictional REDD+
place: global, all jurisdictions eligible for jurisdictional REDD+
data: global remotely sensed forest change data, product not named
method: analysis of jurisdictional baseline approaches, prediction of baseline errors from simple metrics, test for deforestation increases before crediting
finding: Jurisdictional REDD+ baselines let jurisdictions earn credits without new policy, two simple metrics predicted over 30 per cent of baseline errors, and half of enrolled jurisdictions showed pre-crediting deforestation increases.
gap_quote: Given well-known credibility issues in project-based avoided-deforestation credits and over $3 billion in committed credit purchases under ART TREES, the voluntary carbon market is increasingly moving toward jurisdictional approaches to Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD+) as a source of credits.

title: Assessing the Accuracy of Forest Cover Map for 1990, 2000 and 2010 at National Scale in Gabon
data: forest area and forest cover change maps of the ESA GSE Forest Monitoring REDD extension
method: sample-based accuracy assessment of wall-to-wall forest maps
finding: Wall-to-wall forest and change maps for Gabon confirmed low deforestation and exceeded the national agency's requirements, with overall accuracy above 95 per cent.
gap_quote: Initial results confirm the generally low level of deforestation expected in the Congo basin region and in Gabon in particular. However, these results cannot be used without a thorough and statistically sound assessment of thematic accuracy.

title: Deforestation and agriculture in the tropics: carbon emissions and options for mitigation
place: pantropical, 91 countries, with Congo Basin countries named
data: country data on deforestation area and the fraction driven by agriculture, sources not named
method: data-driven emissions estimation with uncertainty propagated from input datasets, decision tree of priority countries, country analysis of large scale land acquisitions
finding: Agriculture-driven deforestation emissions in 91 countries were highest in Latin America, rose in Africa since 1990 led by Congo Basin countries, with uncertainty of plus or minus 62.4 per cent.
gap_quote: Competition for land can result when both these goals are pursued at the same time, because forested land is protected for carbon storage, while agricultural land is expanded (often into forests) to provide sufficient land for growing food.

title: Stem and soil nitrous oxide fluxes from rainforest and cacao agroforest on highly weathered soils in the Congo Basin
place: Cameroon, three sites in central and southern Cameroon, scaled to Congo Basin humid rainforest
data: not stated
method: monthly measurement of stem and soil N2O fluxes in replicate plots, 15N isotope tracing, correlation analysis
finding: Forest conversion to cacao agroforestry did not change N2O fluxes, at 1.55 and 1.15 kg N per ha a year, and tree stems contributed 8 to 38 per cent.
gap_quote: Although tree stems act as conduits for greenhouse gases (GHGs) produced in the soil, the magnitudes of tree contributions to total (soil + stem) nitrous oxide (N 2 O) emissions from tropical rainforests on heavily weathered soils remain unknown.

title: Increasing Forest Disturbance in the Congo Basin is Driven by an Emerging Frontier in Cameroon
place: Congo Basin, six countries, with Cameroon and Democratic Republic of the Congo named
data: Global Forest Change and Tropical Moist Forest datasets, harmonized
method: harmonization of Global Forest Change and Tropical Moist Forest disturbance, linear trend test, overlay with roads and land allocations
predictors: nearness to roads, formal land allocation, community forest, agro-industrial plantation, logging concession
finding: Congo Basin disturbance from 2000 to 2022 was greatest in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, 61,174 km2, but only Cameroon's share rose significantly, by 0.49 per cent a year.
gap_quote: Forest disturbances pose an increasing threat to the ecosystem services provided by tropical forests in the Congo Basin, yet their distribution remains poorly understood.

title: When the Dutch disease met the French connection: oil, macroeconomics and forests in Gabon
data: not stated
method: macroeconomic analysis of oil rent effects on agriculture and forests, with development scenarios
finding: Oil rents in Gabon enabled pro-urban, anti-rural policies that, with low population pressure, shrank agriculture and so protected and possibly expanded forest, more successfully than most deliberate conservation policies.
gap_quote: The gradually emerging decline in Gabon's oil revenues thus poses serious challenges both for the macroeconomy and for forest conservation.

title: Selective logging emissions and potential emission reductions from reduced-impact logging in the Congo Basin
place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Gabon and Republic of the Congo, 23 forest management enterprises
data: field measurements of logging damage under the RIL-C protocol, country logging statistics
method: reduced-impact logging for carbon protocol, models of emissions against biophysical conditions, logging practices and forest policies
predictors: biophysical conditions, logging practices, forest policies, FSC certification
finding: Logging emissions averaged 2.1 Mg C per m3, half avoidable by best RIL-C practice, and Congo Basin selective logging equalled 40 per cent of the region's deforestation emissions.
gap_quote: Emissions from concessions certified by the Forest Stewardship Council (FSC, N = 6) and those that were not certified (N = 17) did not differ.

title: Unveiling Cerrado deforestation: A comparative analysis among Brazilian states
place: Brazil, Cerrado, with Bahia, Maranhão, Tocantins and Piauí named

method: spatio-temporal decomposition of deforestation alerts, land-conversion model of deforested area, logit model of clearing within registered properties

finding: Cerrado clearings were larger in states with simplified licensing, upward trends concentrated in MATOPIBA states, and soybean and pasture expansion raised deforestation risk within registered properties.
gap_quote: The Brazilian Cerrado is one of the world’s most threatened tropical savanna biomes, yet the institutional determinants of deforestation across states remain insufficiently understood.

title: Contact in context: How land use histories, sociocultural practices, and animal profiles shape human-animal contact and zoonotic pathogen exposure in a fragmented forest of the Democratic Republic of Congo
place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, three villages along a forest fragmentation gradient
period: five months of records, years not stated
data: not stated
method: mixed methods, participant diaries of activities and animal contact, cluster analysis, abundance transects, tests of contact frequency, ethnographic and ethnohistorical interviews
predictors: species abundance, human activities, gender, village along the fragmentation gradient
finding: Twenty-four villagers contacted 61 animal species, abundance weakly predicted contact, and contacts reflected decades of land use change, hunting and local categories of disgust rather than ecology alone.
gap_quote: One such factor, human-animal contact, remains poorly understood. Current studies often neglect variability in human-animal engagements across ecological zones and the broader processes bringing people, animals, and pathogens into engagement.

title: A holistic approach to assessing REDD+ forest loss baselines through ex post analysis
data: two geospatial forest loss datasets, one global and one locally calibrated, names not given
method: zone of reasonable accuracy from forest loss rates at several control sites, ex post assessment of project baselines
finding: A zone of reasonable accuracy built from forest loss at control sites found all three Cambodian REDD+ project baselines within or below it, using a global and a local dataset.
gap_quote: Controversy over the reasonableness of such baseline scenarios has thrown this nascent market mechanism into disarray.

title: Small scale agriculture continues to drive deforestation and degradation in fragmented forests in the Congo Basin (2015–2020)
data: remote sensing imagery for visual interpretation, product not named
method: systematically validated visual interpretation of multiple overlapping direct drivers
predictors: small-scale agriculture, villages, roads, mining, industrial forestry, artisanal forestry
finding: In six Central African countries in 2015 to 2020, the rural complex of small-scale agriculture, villages and roads caused most deforestation and degradation, and only artisanal forestry consistently increased.
gap_quote: The Central African region hosts the largest continuous tract of forest in Africa, regulating global climate while providing essential resources and livelihoods for millions of people and harbouring extensive biodiversity. Extractive industries, infrastructure development and industrial agriculture have often been cited as major threats to these forests and are expected to increase.

title: Habitat Suitability Modeling of Endangered Primates in Nigeria: Integrating Satellite Remote Sensing and Spatial Modeling Techniques.
place: Nigeria, Afi-Mbe-Okwangwo protected areas of Cross River State
data: satellite image change detection, sensor not named
method: remote sensing change detection, fragmentation analysis, Markov chain forward simulation, Maxent habitat suitability modelling
finding: Afi-Mbe-Okwangwo deforestation was 1.5 per cent a year in 2000 to 2014, a Markov simulation projected 28,121 ha lost by 2028, and 21 per cent of primate habitat was affected.
gap_quote: These results indicate that suitable primate habitats (particularly for gorillas and chimpanzees) are under immense pressure from deforestation and forest fragmentation.

title: Local Deals for Global Politics
place: Cameroon, Herakles Farms palm oil project
data: not stated
method: qualitative case study of a palm oil project
predictors: limited statehood, bureaucratic capacity and autonomy, transnational companies, western cooperation agencies
finding: Conversion of Cameroon forestland to Herakles Farms palm oil came from erratic state capacity and autonomy combined with strong influence from transnational companies and western cooperation agencies.
gap_quote: International efforts to curtail deforestation and biodiversity loss have increased as agricultural expansion including palm oil production by powerful agribusiness companies has greatly increased. This is particularly the case in tropical regions including Africa where agriculture is taking over forestlands.

title: GEDI observations of foliar height diversity track regrowth trends in the humid tropical forests of the Democratic Republic of Congo
place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, humid tropical forest
data: European Union Tropical Moist Forest product, GEDI foliage height diversity, airborne laser scanning
method: validation of GEDI foliage height diversity against airborne laser scanning, regrowth trajectory of foliage height diversity against forest age
measures: relative root mean square error 10.32 per cent, 5.91 per cent after filtering
finding: Across 7102 regrowing forest locations in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, structural diversity rose fast for about 20 years, then slowly, without recovering by 34 years.
gap_quote: The humid tropical forests of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) cover 1.15 million km 2 and are highly biodiverse but under threat.

title: Curbing Deforestation in the Congo Basin with the Polluter Pays Principle, the Provider Gets Principle and the REDD+ Mechanism
data: not stated
method: not stated
finding: The Congo Basin could curb deforestation from subsistence farming and over logging by adding polluter pays taxes and provider gets payments to REDD+, and more reforestation and enforcement projects.
gap_quote: Projects on afforestation/reforestation are scarce even if the future REDD+ PES scheme will fund those projects. Projects on enforcement of the law or reducing logging are less concerned by the REDD+ mechanism in the Congo Basin.

title: TROPICAL FOREST REMOTE SENSING SERVICES FOR THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO INSIDE THE EU FP7 'RECOVER' PROJECT (FINAL RESULTS 2000-2012)
data: Landsat, ALOS AVNIR-2, RapidEye, Envisat ASAR and ALOS PALSAR mosaics, ICESat GLAS for biomass, Kompsat-2 for validation

measures: accuracy 87 per cent for optical and 88 per cent for radar 2010 forest and non-forest maps
finding: ReCover gave DRC forest and non-forest maps, a 2000 to 2010 forest change map and a biomass map, and 2010 forest maps were 87 and 88 per cent accurate.

title: Estimation of Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Absorption from the Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Use Sector in the Monomodal and Bimodal Rainfall Forest Agroecological Zones of Cameroon
place: Cameroon, monomodal and bimodal rainfall forest agroecological zones
data: images processed in SEPAL and ArcGIS 10.6, sensor not named

finding: From 2010 to 2018, the two zones emitted 281,541.3 Gg CO2 equivalent and absorbed 2,924,841.22, so they absorbed more than they emitted.

title: Forest cover dynamics (1998 to 2019) and prediction of deforestation probability using binary logistic regression (BLR) model of Silabati watershed, India

method: binary logistic regression
predictors: population density, road construction, initiation of cash crops

gap_quote: But in the last few decades, forest areas are being highly converted and depleted due to excessive anthropogenic stress particularly for modern societal development.

title: Scénarii de Réduction des Emissions liées à la Déforestation et la Dégradation forestière en fonction du Niveau des Emissions de Référence pour les Forêts (NERF)
data: Forest Reference Emission Level submitted in 2016
method: emission reduction scenarios set against the Forest Reference Emission Level
finding: Against a Forest Reference Emission Level of 35.5 million t CO2 a year, three reduction scenarios of 8.3, 4.2 and 2.8 million t were proposed, with scenario 2 best suited.

title: Miombo woodland, an ecosystem at risk of disappearance in the Lufira Biosphere Reserve (Upper Katanga, DR Congo)? A 39-years analysis based on Landsat images
place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Lufira Biosphere Reserve, Upper Katanga
data: Landsat images of 1979, 1986, 1998, 2008 and 2018
method: diachronic classification of Landsat images, classifier not named, landscape metrics
finding: Miombo woodland in Lufira Biosphere Reserve fell from 85.3 km2 in 1979 to 11.2 km2 in 2018, deforestation of 1.8 per cent a year, nearly eight times the national rate.
gap_quote: Lufira Biosphere Reserve (LBR) is a protected area located in Southeastern DR Congo, created for the conservation of Miombo woodland, an ecosystem threatened by anthropogenic activities developed in the region. However, scientific studies regarding land cover dynamics within the LBR are non-existent to date.

title: Environmental Impacts of the Oil Palm Cultivation in Cameroon
place: Cameroon, South-West, Littoral and Centre regions
data: satellite images of production basins, sensor not named
method: field surveys, stakeholder workshop resolutions, satellite mapping of oil palm expansion, analysis of four sustainability dimensions
finding: Oil palm, on almost 400,000 ha in Cameroon, became the main driver of deforestation since 1990, expanding greatly under inadequate policy, while production rose from 150,000 to 413,000 t.
gap_quote: Since 1990, oil palm cultivation, because nibbling large zones in dense forest areas of Cameroon, becomes the main driver of deforestation. It leads to the loss of plant and animal biodiversity as well as engaging soils and water pollution, which raises questions about its sustainability.

title: Hierarchical Analysis of Miombo Woodland Spatial Dynamics in Lualaba Province (Democratic Republic of the Congo), 1990–2024: Integrating Remote Sensing and Landscape Ecology Techniques
place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Lualaba Province, five territories and protected areas
data: Landsat images
method: random forest classification, landscape metrics at province, territory and protected area levels
predictors: dominant land use of territory, agriculture or mining, protected area status
finding: Lualaba Miombo woodland cover fell from 62.9 to under 25 per cent from 1990 to 2024, most in agricultural territories, with significant deforestation inside protected areas.
gap_quote: Lualaba Province, located in the southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), consists of five territories with varied dominant land uses: agriculture (Dilolo, Kapanga, and Musumba in the west) and mining (Mutshatsha and Lubudi in the east). The province also includes protected areas with significant governance challenges.

title: Land-use change drives present and future distributions of Fall armyworm, Spodoptera frugiperda (J.E. Smith) (Lepidoptera: Noctuidae).
place: global, with central Africa among high suitability areas
period: present and future under RCP 2.6 and 8.5, year not stated
data: land use, topography and climate layers, products not named
method: MaxEnt species distribution models under RCP 2.6 and 8.5 scenarios
predictors: land use, topography, climate, crop type
finding: MaxEnt models showed land use change shaped fall armyworm distribution more than climate, with high potential habitat including central Africa and the largest future threat increase in Africa.
gap_quote: However, to date, few studies have simulated the future distribution patterns of fall armyworm under rapid global changes.

title: Characterizing Spectral Signatures for Forest Cover and Change Using Field Data: A Case-Study of Kimvula Territory in Democratic Republic of Congo from 2000 to 2010
place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kimvula Territory
data: USAID CARPE forest cover map, Landsat ETM+ reflectance, field observations of tree height and circumference
method: field validation of an existing forest cover and change map, analysis of Landsat ETM+ band reflectance against field data
finding: Field data checked the CARPE forest cover map for 2000 to 2010 and identified the best Landsat bands for deforestation, but Landsat poorly separated primary from mature regrowing forest.
gap_quote: Despite their importance, several authors have shown global evidence of deforestation, especially in the tropics.

title: Spatial modeling of the potential of agricultural or forestry production for sustainable land use planning
place: Congo Basin, Cameroon, Gabon, Republic of the Congo, Democratic Republic of the Congo and Central African Republic
data: not stated
method: stepwise mapping of land suitable for oil palm under RSPO principles and criteria, evaluation of production models
validation: compared with national park agency maps of conservation importance in Gabon
finding: Maps of land suitable for sustainable RSPO palm oil in five Congo Basin countries were consistent with Gabon's conservation maps and used in Republic of the Congo REDD+ discussions.
gap_quote: Such plans for agricultural development also present threats such as deforestation, loss of biodiversity and land use conflicts, and caution and planning are needed to avoid negative social and environmental impacts.

title: The fast and the focused: Balancing timely and accurate classification of deforestation and degradation drivers using remote sensing
data: satellite images up to four years after forest loss events, sensor not named
method: Cam-ForestNet deep learning classification of fifteen direct drivers, single-date compared with multi-year imagery
validation: evaluation on labelled forest loss events, method not stated
measures: macro-average and per-class F1 scores, values not stated
finding: Combining images up to four years after forest loss raised Cam-ForestNet driver classification F1 for nearly all classes, but a single first-year image performed best among single images.
gap_quote: Identifying drivers of deforestation is crucial for developing targeted conservation and land management strategies, and satellite data provide a long time series of data to understand deforestation dynamics. However, the timing of imagery after forest loss may affect classification accuracy, and optimal timing may be different for different drivers.

title: Challenges to Sustainable Forest Management and Community Livelihoods Sustenance in Cameroon: Evidence from the Southern Bakundu Forest Reserve in Southwest Cameroon
place: Cameroon, Southern Bakundu Forest Reserve, Southwest Region
data: not stated
method: questionnaire survey of rated local trigger forces
predictors: scarcity of farmland outside the reserve, population growth, poverty, higher fertility of reserve land
finding: Farmland scarcity, population growth, poverty and fertile reserve soils drove deforestation in the Southern Bakundu reserve, and corrupt complicity and scarce resources hampered forest monitoring.
gap_quote: Sustainable forest management in Cameroon is being plagued with many challenges directly related to key issues in the areas of forest law enforcement and governance.

title: Using real-time forest loss alerts and global deforestation maps to assess the effectiveness of Africa's tropical protected areas
place: Africa, 224 parks in 23 countries, with Central Africa named
data: high resolution satellite forest loss data, alerts and global deforestation maps, products not named
method: comparison of forest loss inside and outside parks
predictors: park size, park age, IUCN management category, region
finding: Most of 224 African parks curbed forest loss, larger and younger parks more so, and Central African parks lost least forest inside their boundaries and West African parks most.
gap_quote: Having undergone rapid changes in forest cover over the last two decades, a large amount of irreplaceable biodiversity has been lost.

title: Global forecasts of urban expansion to 2030 and direct impacts on biodiversity and carbon pools
place: global, with Eastern Afromontane, Guinean Forests of West Africa, and Western Ghats and Sri Lanka hotspots named
data: global urban land cover circa 2000, product not named
method: spatially explicit probabilistic forecasts of urban land cover change
finding: Urban land cover was forecast to grow by 1.2 million km2 by 2030, nearly tripling, removing 1.38 PgC of pantropical vegetation biomass, about 5 per cent of tropical deforestation emissions.
gap_quote: Urban land-cover change threatens biodiversity and affects ecosystem productivity through loss of habitat, biomass, and carbon storage. However, despite projections that world urban populations will increase to nearly 5 billion by 2030, little is known about future locations, magnitudes, and rates of urban expansion.

title: Near-Real-Time African Tropical Forest Loss Monitoring with Sentinel-1 data: From Threshold-Based to Deep Learning Detection
place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Dekese for training and Likati for validation
data: temporally standardized Sentinel-1 C-band SAR
method: random forest, multi-layer perceptron and U-Net convolutional neural network detection over a 24-day sliding window
validation: applied and validated at a distinct site 800 km from training
finding: A Sentinel-1 forest loss detector moved from random forest to multi-layer perceptron and U-Net, trained at Dekese and validated 800 km away at Likati, with no accuracy given.
gap_quote: Nevertheless, annual assessments based on optical imagery tend to show their limits in the African tropical forests, where the semi-persistent cloud cover prevents the proper detection of short-duration and small-scale events.

title: Identifying areas of deforestation risk for REDD+ using a species modeling tool
data: forest cover loss for 2000 to 2009, source not named, carbon density values
method: Maximum Entropy Modelling of deforestation risk, linked to carbon density to estimate emissions
predictors: accessibility, distance to previous deforestation, land use designation
validation: predicted risk compared with observed deforestation
finding: Maxent deforestation risk for Madre de Dios had AUC above 0.9, led by accessibility and distance to past loss, and projected 132,865 ha lost by 2020.
gap_quote: Each comes with its own methodological challenges, and existing approaches and tools to do so can be costly to implement or require considerable technical knowledge and skill.

title: Modeling deforestation risk in the Maya Biosphere Reserve, Guatemala
place: Guatemala, Maya Biosphere Reserve and buffer zone
data: existing GIS databases and remote sensing data
method: spatial and statistical analysis of each factor, combined into a deterministic deforestation risk model
finding: Roads, settlements and soil quality each explained part of deforestation in the Maya Biosphere Reserve and were combined into a deterministic risk model for policy scenarios, with no values given.
gap_quote: The tropical forest of Guatemala's 21,130 square kilometer Maya Biosphere Reserve and buffer zone is being impacted by deforestation due to an increase of the local population and establishment of over 200 new settlements over the last 20 years.

title: "Community Perception of Landslide Hazards and Settlement Expansion along the North-West Stretch of the Cameroon Volcanic Line"
place: Cameroon, Bamenda escarpment on the North-West stretch of the Cameroon Volcanic Line
data: satellite imagery, sensor not named
method: mixed methods, multi-stage random sampling survey, remote sensing and GIS mapping of land use change, chi-square tests and simple linear regression
finding: Built-up area on the 8.4 km2 Bamenda escarpment grew markedly from 1980 to 2020, perception of landslide risk varied with age, education and income, and coping measures were largely ineffective.
gap_quote: The Bamenda escarpment, a geologically sensitive region located along the North-West stretch of the Cameroon Volcanic Line, spans approximately 8.4km² and is characterized by steep slopes and highly weathered residual soils.These features make the area highly prone to landslides, especially during the rainy season.

title: Tracing the trail of eroded fertile soils during a high intensity rainfall event: A fingerprinting study in war-torn tropical mountains.
place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, catchment on the Lake Kivu shore
period: one storm event, year not stated
data: sediment samples from four land use and land cover source types, no map named
method: sediment fingerprinting of source samples, fluvial terrace targets and a delta gravity core
predictors: land use and land cover source type, discharge
finding: Channel banks and degraded areas supplied more sediment as discharge rose, but cropland and banana plantations supplied most fine sediment exported to Lake Kivu.
gap_quote: To better understand such dynamics, we investigated an agricultural mountainous catchment located on the Democratic Republic of the Congo shore of Lake Kivu. This area is characterised by weak governance systems exacerbated by protracted violent conflicts, which have prevented the application of remediation practices to address extensive land use changes, including deforestation and monoculture proliferation, notably banana plantations.

title: Large underestimation of smallholder agriculture in the tropics by classic remote sensing products: evidenced from the Kasaï River Basin
data: 3,734 reference observations, AlphaEarth Foundations embeddings of multi-source Earth observation data, global land cover products for comparison
method: random forest classification of AlphaEarth Foundations embeddings, transition analysis
validation: reference observations, compared with global land cover products
measures: accuracy 96 to 100 per cent for urban and water, 74 to 87 per cent for forest, savanna and cropland, against 30 to 65 per cent for global products
finding: Regional 30 m mapping put 2024 cropland at 16.2 per cent of the Kasaï basin, against 0.1 to 4.7 per cent in global products, with 53,128 km2 converted since 2017.
gap_quote: The Kasaï River Basin (KRB), the largest tributary system of the Congo basin, is undergoing rapid land-use transformation driven by population growth and expanding economic activities. However, existing global and regional land-cover products do not fully capture this highly heterogeneous, smallholder-dominated landscape or its temporal dynamics.

title: Consistent Pantropical Deforestation Monitoring in Dense Humid Forests from Landsat Time Series (2000–2025)
place: pantropical, Amazonia, Central Africa, Southeast Asia
data: Landsat Analysis Ready Data, intact tropical forest masks, Global Forest Change and Tropical Moist Forest products
method: Normalized Burn Ratio time series change detection with local standardization, adaptive cloud masking and spatial and temporal refinement
validation: two-level validation framework combining spatial intersections and temporal stratification, compared with widely used global datasets
measures: bias, value not stated, root mean square error, value not stated
finding: A Landsat Normalized Burn Ratio time series method reduced bias and root mean square error in annual deforestation estimates relative to global datasets, most clearly in the Congo Basin.
gap_quote: These challenges are most pronounced in regions such as the Congo Basin, where observational limitations lead to uneven detection performance and reduced comparability across datasets.

title: CARBONISATION ET DÉFORESTATION À KASANGULU (RDC) : DYNAMIQUES, ENJEUX DE DURABILITÉ ET PERSPECTIVES SOCIO ENVIRONNEMENTALES
place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kongo Central, Kasangulu territory
data: Landsat and Sentinel imagery
method: mixed methods of Landsat and Sentinel remote sensing, a survey of 210 households and qualitative interviews
finding: Miombo woodland area fell 33 per cent from 2000 to 2025, at 1.91 per cent a year in 2013 to 2025, and charcoal production accounted for about 60 per cent.
gap_quote: Despite a strong awareness of forest decline, attempts to adopt improved kilns or reforestation largely fail (>80% abandonment rate) due to economic, land tenure, and technical constraints.

title: Change Detection and Remote Sensing Methodologies to Track Deforestation and Growth in Threatened Global Rainforests
place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Indonesia, Peru
data: Landsat 5 and 7 Thematic Mapper, MODIS Vegetation Continuous Fields, Landsat VCF
method: supervised maximum likelihood classification and MODIS VCF guided forest and non-forest masking, with k-nearest-neighbour classification and post-classification image differencing
validation: accuracy assessment with 500 validation pixels at each study area, compared with Landsat VCF
finding: Forest and non-forest masking guided by MODIS VCF had the highest overall accuracy and labelled change best, while Landsat VCF overestimated forest cover at all three sites.
gap_quote: Conventional Supervised Classification had slightly lower overall accuracy but performed poorly when labeling change areas.

title: The Impact of Land Cover Changes Surrounding Meteorological Stations on Measurements and Observations Using Landsat Satellite Data
data: GLanCE 2001 to 2019, GLC_FCS30D 1985 to 2022
method: land cover change analysis within 1, 2, 10 and 30 km radii and wind sectors, homogeneity tests, machine learning anomaly detection
finding: The abstract stated no result. Land cover change was analysed around 62 Polish synoptic stations from 1985 to 2022 with GLanCE and GLC_FCS30D.
gap_quote: Changes in land cover around a meteorological station can influence measurement outcomes, thereby compromising the homogeneity of climatic data.

title: Understanding deforestation dynamics in Amazonian protected areas through land-use change models informed by conservation discourses
place: Brazil, Jamanxim National Forest, Bolivia, Amboró and Carrasco National Parks, Peru, Tambopata National Reserve and Bahuaja-Sonene National Park
data: not stated
method: land use change models integrating quantitative and qualitative analysis of conservation discourses
predictors: slope, population density, surrounding non-forest, proximity to agriculture, proximity to fires, legal threats to protected area status, payments for ecosystem services projects, REDD+ projects
validation: compared with standard land use change models
finding: Models informed by conservation discourses outperformed standard land use change models, with deforestation higher near agriculture and fires, and lower on steep slopes and at high population density.
gap_quote: Responses to PA deforestation require understanding the region-wide and PA-specific socio-environmental factors that increase forest conversion.

title: Global economic trade-offs between wild nature and tropical agriculture
data: not stated
method: spatially explicit trade-off analysis combining GIS with a meta-analysis of ecosystem service studies
finding: Externalities of tropical deforestation exceeded direct agricultural benefits unless high-value crop potentials were realised, and conversion appeared economically efficient in the Atlantic Forest, Gulf of Guinea and Thailand.
gap_quote: Much of this deforestation occurs with a lack of information on the spatial distribution of benefits and costs of deforestation.

title: Urban Growth and Front Development on Risk Zones: GIS Application for Mapping of Impacts on Yaounde North Western Highlands, Cameroon
place: Cameroon, Yaounde north western highlands, Mbankolo, Febe, Carrier, Nkolbisson, Messa
data: satellite images of different periods, GPS data, topographic maps
method: GIS mapping from satellite images, GPS data, field observations, surveys and documents
finding: Displaced poor urban dwellers occupied risk-prone areas of north west Yaounde, where uncontrolled deforestation, wetland occupation and soil degradation for settlement and farming were high.
gap_quote: African cities today are confronted with the problem of rapid urbanisation, poverty and land use abuse. Yaounde, the political capital of Cameroon is a victim of this situation.

title: La protection des forets tropicales ombrophiles de l'Afrique
data: not stated
method: not stated
finding: The report argued that rainforest loss in West and Central Africa, almost 2 million hectares a year, was alarming and needed halting soon through an integrated development approach.
gap_quote: The speed with which tropical rainforests in West and Central Africa are disappearing is alarming - almost 2 million hectares of tropical forests are lost each year.

title: Lake Tanganyika Biodiversity Project Special Study on Sediment Discharge and its Consequences: Soil Erosion Modelling in the Lake Tanganyika Catchment
place: Lake Tanganyika catchment, Burundi, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Tanzania

finding: Three catchment regions, in Burundi, Democratic Republic of the Congo and Tanzania, were particularly sensitive to erosion, with near total deforestation and high sediment entry in Burundi.
gap_quote: The results suggest that there are three regions of the lake catchment (one each in Burundi, Zaire and Tanzania) that are particularly sensitive to erosion.

title: Anthropogenic land-use change shapes zoonotic risk in terrestrial small mammals from Maniema, Democratic Republic of Congo
place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Maniema Province
data: not stated
method: molecular screening for DNA of five pathogen groups, comparison of prevalence between villages and forest plots, phylogenetic analysis

finding: Bartonella, found in 22 per cent of samples from 380 small mammals, was more common in villages, while Hepatozoon, Anaplasmataceae and herpesviruses were more common in forest hosts.
gap_quote: Human-driven environmental change is increasingly recognized as a major driver of emerging infectious diseases.

title: Beyond deforestation metrics: agricultural landscape archetypes derived from earth observation reveal forest and savannah frontier dynamics in the Republic of Congo
data: harmonized national land use and land cover maps combining TMF, GLAD and ESA CCI-LC, at five-year intervals

finding: Seven agricultural landscape archetypes were identified across forest, forest and savannah mosaic, and savannah landscapes, following socio-economic gradients and showing frontier patterns that national deforestation statistics miss.
gap_quote: Agricultural expansion is reshaping the forest and savannah landscapes of the Congo Basin, yet the spatial organization of these transformations remains poorly documented.

title: Lion Conservation Amid Climate and Land-Use Change: Insights from a West-Central Africa Distribution Model
period: 1900 to 1990 and 1981 to 2010, projected to 2041 to 2070, land use projected to 2050

finding: Models showed climatically suitable lion habitat expanding under current and future climates, while human pressures, not climate, severely constrained the actual distribution.
gap_quote: The African lion (Panthera leo) has experienced catastrophic range contraction, with West and Central Africa suffering a 93% population decline and lions now occupying just 1.1% of their historical West African range.

title: Choice of ex-post deforestation baseline methodology critically affects assessments of REDD+ project performance
data: not stated

gap_quote: Traditionally, baselines are estimated ex-ante by extrapolating historical deforestation trends, but this approach has been criticised for subjectivity and inadequately capturing changing deforestation pressures, leading to ex-post counterfactual techniques being forwarded as more objective alternatives.

title: Road Networks and Tropical Deforestation
data: not stated

gap_quote: We find that Brazil's extensive existing road network increases this required transfer, demonstrating how infrastructure creates ``deforestation lock-in'' that makes conservation progressively more expensive.

title: Effects of choice in land cover data on ecosystem service mapping in data-scarce regions
data: eight open access global land use and land cover products
method: InVEST Sediment Delivery Ratio model, uncertainty propagation across eight land cover products, hotspot agreement analysis
predictors: land use and land cover, precipitation
finding: No global land cover product reached 60 per cent accuracy, the eight products disagreed on the direction of net change, and erosion control hotspots agreed poorly, Pearson r 0.12.
gap_quote: Accurate ecosystem services modeling is critical for sustainable development in the Congo Basin and requires reliable land cover and land use (LULC) data, yet data-scarcity in the region results in a reliance on global LULC products.

title: Global Land cover Mapping and Estimation (GLanCE): a record of land cover and land cover change at Landsat scale across decades
place: global, Americas, Europe, Africa, Asia and Oceania
data: Landsat classification from the complete archive, with multi-source global training data
method: Continuous Change Detection and Classification algorithm, iterative sub-continental machine learning classification
validation: accuracy assessment against primary and secondary reference labels
measures: continental accuracy 75 to 94 per cent across years, user's and producer's accuracies mostly above 80 per cent for tree, water and herbaceous classes and above 60 per cent for developed, variable for shrub and barren
finding: The first global GLanCE release gave annual Landsat land cover, change and EVI2 metrics over decades in seven classes, with continental accuracies of 75 to 94 per cent.
gap_quote: Recent global land cover products derived from Sentinel-2 data, including ESA WorldCover, ESRI's land use and land cover product, and Google's Dynamic World, offer high-quality information but are temporally limited to approximately the last decade.

title: Kinshasa and Climate Change: How Population Growth Exacerbates Vulnerability
place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kinshasa, Mont-Ngafula and Ngaliema
data: not stated
method: critical framework of land governance, illustrative heuristic representation, three prospective pathways to 2050
finding: Population growth of about 4 per cent a year, unplanned urbanization and stronger hydrological extremes drove Kinshasa's vulnerability, with deforestation for housing and energy a plausible but uncertain contributor.
gap_quote: Kinshasa's climate vulnerability stems not solely from climate change but from the convergence of sustained population growth (≈ 4%/year), unplanned urbanization, and the intensification of hydrological extremes.

title: Mapping Land Degradation and Mining Expansion in Colomine, Cameroon Using Random Forest Classification and Multi-Temporal Sentinel-2 Imagery
data: Sentinel-2 classification for 2015, 2020 and 2025
method: random forest classification, post-classification change detection, transition matrix, UNCCD Land Degradation Neutrality framework
measures: overall accuracy 97.41 to 99.49 per cent, Kappa 0.961 to 0.993
finding: From 2015 to 2025, vegetation fell 34.52 per cent and bare land grew 247.54 per cent, with 31.65 per cent of the area degraded and 7.03 per cent improved.
gap_quote: Artisanal and small-scale mining (ASM) has become a major driver of land degradation in eastern Cameroon.

title: Increasing Fire Activity in African Tropical Forests Is Associated With Deforestation and Climate Change
place: West and Central Africa tropical forests, Congo Basin
data: Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer active fires, deforestation data not stated
method: trend analysis of active fire detections
finding: Fires in African tropical forests mostly rose over 2003 to 2021, chiefly in the northeastern and southern Congo Basin and in high deforestation areas, tracking temperature and vapor pressure deficit.
gap_quote: Fires were historically rare in tropical forests of West and Central Africa, where dense vegetation, rapid decomposition, and high moisture limit available fuels. However, increasing heat and drought combined with forest degradation and fragmentation are making these areas more susceptible to wildfires.

title: Increasing pressure on protected areas in the DR Congo
data: not stated
method: quasi-experimental methods, typology of protection by spatio-temporal context
predictors: protected area protection, spatio-temporal context of protection
finding: Many protected areas in the Democratic Republic of the Congo were found unable to hold back deforestation at their boundaries, as the passive protection of remoteness faded.
gap_quote: As this passive protection begins to fade with the progression of deforestation frontiers, the future role of PAs in conserving the Congo Basin rainforest is uncertain.

title: Assessing data availability for the development of REDD-plus national reference levels
data: not stated
method: comparison of historical, forest-trend and business-as-usual reference levels
validation: three reference level types compared with each other
finding: In Thailand, historical, forest-trend and business-as-usual reference levels gave different future deforestation estimates, so countries should choose a reference level, simple to complex, matching their data availability.
gap_quote: Data availability in developing countries is known to be extremely varied and is one of the constraints for setting the national reference levels (RLs) for the REDD-plus

title: L'Impact de la crise economique sur les systemes agricoles et la changement du couvert forestier dans la zone forestiere humide du Cameroun
data: household survey of 648 households in 54 villages
method: household sample survey testing four hypotheses
predictors: economic crisis, 1994 currency devaluation, plantation and food crop balance, market orientation of food crops, gender division of labour, dependence on non-timber forest products
finding: In Cameroon's humid forest zone, smallholders responded to the economic crisis and 1994 devaluation by shifting toward market food crops, and their rate of forest clearing increased overall.
gap_quote: The study concludes that economic crises and macroeconomic policies can have unexpected and powerful effects on land use and forest practices. Future policies aimed at improving forest conservation and management must take account of this fact.

title: Tropical protected areas reduced deforestation carbon emissions by one third from 2000–2012
data: not stated
method: emissions avoided against expected deforestation controlling for spatial variation in deforestation pressure
predictors: protected area status, deforestation pressure, protected area designation
finding: Tropical protected areas reduced deforestation carbon emissions by 4.88 Pg, about 29 per cent, in 2000 to 2012, led by the Americas, with Africa contributing 12.7 TgC per year.
gap_quote: While the effectiveness of PAs in reducing deforestation has been estimated, the impact on global carbon emissions remains unquantified.

title: The Impacts of Oil Palm on Recent Deforestation and Biodiversity Loss
place: pantropical, 20 countries in Southeast Asia, South America, Mesoamerica and Africa
data: Google Earth high-resolution imagery, Landsat, FAO oil palm planted area
method: visual assessment of sample areas, comparison with FAO planted area trends, oil palm suitability mapping of vulnerable forests
validation: compared with FAO oil palm planted area trends
finding: Of sampled plantations, 45 per cent in Southeast Asia and 7 per cent in Africa replaced 1989 forest, and Africa and South America held the largest vulnerable forest areas.
gap_quote: The conversion to date, and future expansion, threatens biodiversity and increases greenhouse gas emissions.

title: Predictive Modelling of Land Cover Changes in the Greater Amanzule Peatlands Using Multi-Source Remote Sensing and Machine Learning Techniques
data: Landsat-7, Landsat-8, ALOS PALSAR, Shuttle Radar Topography Mission digital elevation models
method: random forest classification, cellular automata artificial neural networks
validation: classification accuracy assessment and predictive model validation, design not stated
measures: overall accuracy 93 per cent in 2010 and 94 per cent in 2015 and 2020, weighted F1 80.0, 75.8 and 75.7 per cent, prediction Kappa 0.70, prediction overall accuracy 80 per cent
finding: Peatland cover grew 12 per cent, rubber plantations 85 per cent, and natural forest fell 6 per cent over 2010 to 2020, with little change projected to 2040.
gap_quote: The Greater Amanzule Peatlands (GAP) in Ghana is an important biodiversity hotspot facing increasing pressure from anthropogenic land-use activities driven by rapid agricultural plantation expansion, urbanisation, and the burgeoning oil and gas industry. Accurate measurement of how these pressures alter land cover over time, along with the projection of future changes, is crucial for sustainable management.

title: Temporal standardization of Sentinel-1 time series for annual and continuous tropical forest loss detection
data: Sentinel-1A C-band synthetic aperture radar ground range detected time series
method: temporal standardization of Sentinel-1 backscatter into pixel z-values, annual and continuous threshold detection
validation: performance metric ensemble for rare class detection, annual and continuous methods compared
measures: annual detection 96.5 per cent of forest loss area, annual false positive rate in stable forest 0.04 per cent, continuous detection 98.3 per cent, false positive rate 0.05 per cent
finding: Standardized Sentinel-1 data detected 96.5 per cent of annual and 98.3 per cent of continuous forest loss area, with false positive rates of 0.04 and 0.05 per cent.
gap_quote: Nevertheless, yearly assessments using optical images tend to face challenges in African moist tropical forests, where the semi-persistent cloud coverage prevents short-term and small-scale events from being correctly detected.

title: Quantifying Forest Loss in the Mbalmayo Forest Reserve (Center Region, Cameroon)
place: Cameroon, Center Region, Mbalmayo forest reserve
data: Landsat 5 TM, 7 ETM+ and 8 OLI images of 1990, 2005 and 2020
method: image classification in ArcGIS and Erdas Imagine, ethnobotanical surveys
finding: The Mbalmayo reserve lost 6993 ha of forest, 26.92 per cent, over 1990 to 2020, averaging 233.1 ha per year, with more loss in 1990 to 2005.
gap_quote: Therefore, it becomes urgent to redefine a management plan for the Mbalmayo forest reserve which will define how the forest must be managed in order to avoid the loss of large areas of forests disappearing each year under the human action, which exerts pressure on forest species, thus leading to their possible disappearance.

title: Methodological issues with deforestation baselines compromise the integrity of carbon offsets from REDD+
place: four VCS-certified REDD+ project areas, not named
data: not stated
method: alternative deforestation baselines built under four VCS-REDD+ methodologies
validation: baselines from four methodologies compared with each other
measures: highest to lowest baseline ratio above 14, averaged over projects
finding: Baselines built for four VCS-certified projects under the four VCS-REDD+ methodologies differed widely, the highest averaging over 14 times the lowest, which questions the additionality of the offsets.
gap_quote: Deforestation baselines are inconsistent across REDD+ methodologies.

title: Global data and tools for local forest cover loss and REDD+ performance assessment: Accuracy, uncertainty, complementarity and impact
place: five local REDD+ initiatives in four tropical countries, not named
data: a global forest cover change dataset, open-source break detection on Landsat time series, high-resolution optical imagery
method: open-source break detection algorithm, dataset combination strategies, sample-based area estimation
validation: validation sample interpreted from Landsat time series and high-resolution imagery
measures: user's accuracy, value not stated, producer's accuracy, value not stated
finding: Global and locally modifiable forest change data differed in accuracy by site, combined products validated by samples were advantageous, and REDD+ performance stayed statistically uncertain in most cases.
gap_quote: Still, these datasets and tools are not always consistent or complementary, and their suitability for local REDD+ performance assessments remains unclear.

title: Mapping Forest Degradation due to Selective Logging by Means of Time Series Analysis: Case Studies in Central Africa
place: Cameroon and Central African Republic, two study sites
data: Landsat time series
method: Landsat time series analysis with spectral mixture analysis and classification of spectral curves
validation: visual interpretation of very high-resolution optical imagery
measures: overall accuracy above 85 per cent at both sites
finding: A Landsat time series method mapped selective logging degradation in Cameroon and the Central African Republic with overall accuracy above 85 per cent at both sites.
gap_quote: However, remote-sensing-based detection of forest degradation is difficult, as these subtle degradation signals are not easy to detect in the first place and quickly lost over time due to fast re-vegetation.

title: Comparing climate and cost impacts of reference levels for reducing emissions from deforestation
data: not stated
method: stylized partial equilibrium model OSIRIS, the open source impacts of REDD incentives spreadsheet
predictors: national incentives to participate, international leakage of deforestation emissions
finding: Across six reference level designs, REDD gave cost-efficient mitigation, the best designs balancing incentives for high and low historical deforesters, while leakage from frontier agriculture strongly affected the estimates.
gap_quote: Estimates of emission reductions under REDD depend critically on the degree to which demand for tropical frontier agriculture generates leakage.

title: Towards performance assessment of subnational forest-based climate change mitigation initiatives
data: not stated
method: not stated
finding: The abstract gave no result, arguing that hundreds of subnational REDD+ initiatives offered a chance to develop and compare methods for quantifying their carbon impacts.
gap_quote: The central role of forests in climate change mitigation, as recognized in the Paris agreement, makes it important to develop and test methods for monitoring and evaluating the carbon e ectiveness of e orts that aim to reduce emissions from deforestation and forest degradation and enhance carbon stocks (REDD+).

title: A global evaluation of the effectiveness of voluntary REDD+ projects at reducing deforestation and degradation in the moist tropics
place: moist tropics, 40 VCS-certified REDD+ projects in 9 countries
period: first 5 years of implementation, years not stated
data: a new tropical humid forest data set
method: standardized evaluation by pixel matching
finding: Over their first five years, 40 VCS REDD+ projects reduced deforestation by 47 per cent and degradation by 58 per cent against matched pixels, with little leakage within 10 km.
gap_quote: Reducing emissions from deforestation and forest degradation (REDD+) projects aim to contribute to climate change mitigation by protecting and enhancing carbon stocks in tropical forests, but there have been no systematic global evaluations of their impact.

title: It’s still Hungry People and Mining – Deforestation in Kahuzi-Biega National Park - Eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo
place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kahuzi-Biega National Park
data: high-resolution satellite imagery, Landsat-based deforestation data products, two field visits
method: interpretation of high-resolution imagery and Landsat-based deforestation products with field visits
finding: Deforestation in Kahuzi-Biega National Park, mostly from farming and some mining, rose from 1.40 to 5.58 per cent over 2013 to 2023, worst in the highlands.
gap_quote: Deforestation is worsening steadily (1.40 to 5.58 percent from 2013 to 2023) and is especially acute in the highland part of the park which is home to Grauer’s gorillas.

title: Baseline choice and performance implications for REDD
data: not stated
method: dynamic model of land conversion from forest to agriculture
finding: In a dynamic land conversion model, none of four REDD baselines dominated, a forward-looking baseline improved on the historical average, and a corridor baseline kept incentives during high opportunity costs.
gap_quote: We show that none of the analysed baselines dominates in all performance aspects, and that the final baseline choice needs to maximise the trade-off between the effectiveness to reduce deforestation, cost-efficiency, and changes in income.

title: Small forest patches in West Africa: mapping how they are changing to better inform their conservation
place: Togo, Benin, Nigeria and Cameroon, Guinean savannah and humid Guineo-Congolian regions
data: not stated
method: patch-based analysis of number, area, rate and trend of forest loss, extrapolation of current loss rate
predictors: patch size, primary or secondary forest type
finding: Small forest patches shrank over 2000 to 2022 at rising loss rates, fastest in small primary patches, and 14 per cent of mapped forest could be lost by 2032.
gap_quote: Forest patches <100 ha have not been widely catalogued before; we mapped forest loss of small forest patches outside of protected areas in the Guinean savannah and humid Guineo-Congolian bioclimatic regions of Togo, Benin, Nigeria and Cameroon between 2000 and 2022.

title: Modeling the Spatial Transition Probabilities of Landscape Dynamics in an Amazonian Colonization Frontier
data: not stated
method: spatial transition probability modelling of landscape dynamics
finding: The abstract gave no result, arguing that understanding Amazon landscape dynamics required accurate measurement of change and its spatial trends to evaluate possible paths of the region.
gap_quote: Many researchers concerned about the enormous ecological impact of deforestation in the Amazon have turned their attention to this rich biome, which is the largest tropical forest in the world.

title: Applying the conservativeness principle to REDD to deal with the uncertainties of the estimates
data: not stated
method: conservativeness principle from UNFCCC decisions and IPCC guidance
finding: Concepts and tools already in UNFCCC decisions and IPCC guidance, chiefly conservativeness, could greatly help deal with the uncertainty of estimated emission reductions from reduced deforestation.
gap_quote: high uncertainties in input data—i.e., area change and C stock change/area—may seriously undermine the credibility of the estimates and therefore of reduced deforestation as a mitigation option.

title: Mapping Process to Pattern in the Landscape Change of the Amazonian Frontier
data: not stated
method: household-level model of forest dynamics integrating deforestation and forest succession
finding: A household-level model joining deforestation and secondary forest succession, driven partly by household characteristics, accounted for the spatial pattern of deforestation seen on Amazon colonization frontiers.

title: How Can Remote Sensing Help Monitor Tropical Moist Forest Degradation?—A Systematic Review
data: not stated
method: systematic review
finding: Remote sensing studies of moist tropical forest degradation were few, especially in the Congo Basin and Southeast Asia, and forest structure was easiest to measure, composition and regeneration harder.
gap_quote: Tropical moist forest degradation is not extensively studied especially in the Congo basin and in southeast Asia.

title: Has global deforestation accelerated due to the COVID-19 pandemic?
place: pantropical, Americas, Africa and Asia, Brazil, Colombia, Peru, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Indonesia
data: Terra-i pantropical land cover change monitoring system
method: time series analysis projecting expected 2020 deforestation from 2004 to 2019 trends
predictors: historical deforestation trend, onset of COVID-19 cases
finding: Observed 2020 deforestation departed from Terra-i projected trends in some countries such as Peru but not in others such as Brazil and Indonesia after the first COVID-19 cases.
gap_quote: As the COVID-19 pandemic unfolded, questions arose as to whether the pandemic would amplify or pacify tropical deforestation. Early reports warned of increased deforestation rates; however, these studies were limited to a few months in 2020 or to selected regions.

title: Is the Climate of the Congo basin Becoming Less Able to Support a Tropical Forest Ecosystem?
place: Congo Basin rain forest and its margins, coastal Angola
data: ERA5 reanalysis climate data, forest change data not stated
method: modified Centro de Previsao de Tempo e Estudios Climaticos potential vegetation model forced by ERA5
predictors: decadal climate states, meridional moisture gradients, low-level westerly moisture transport, sea surface temperatures
finding: From the 1980s to the 2010s, climate at the northern and southern Congo Basin forest margins and along interior transport routes became less able to support rain forest.
gap_quote: Ongoing degradation of the Congolese rain forest is documented, but the individual roles of climate change and deforestation are unknown.

title: Investigating the Effect of Trade Openness and Agriculture on Deforestation in Cameroon
data: World Bank and FAO data
method: fully modified ordinary least squares
predictors: trade openness, agricultural output, agricultural value-added, GDP, GDP squared
finding: In Cameroon over 1980 to 2021, agricultural output and value-added raised deforestation, trade openness raised it until a threshold, and income showed an environmental Kuznets curve.
gap_quote: We recommend the implementation of concrete actions and strict environmental policies focused on a green economy, to control the exploitation of natural resources with particular attention to the sustainable exploitation of wood.

title: Land use/land cover change-induced greenhouse gas emissions in the global biosphere reserve of tropical Afromontane forest
place: Sheka Forest Biosphere Reserve, tropical Afromontane forest, country not stated
data: not stated
method: IPCC Tier 1 approach
finding: Emissions from land use change in the Sheka reserve rose from 0.4 to 5.2 tonnes CO2e per hectare per year over 1999 to 2020, mainly from deforestation and forest degradation.
gap_quote: Land use/land cover (LULC) change is a prominent problem and source of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in tropical forests. However, little to no evidence is available on the contribution of biosphere reserves to reversing LULC change trajectories and reducing GHG emissions, particularly in tropical Afromontane forests.

title: What Role for Tropical Forests in Climate Change Mitigation? The Case of Costa Rica
data: Costa Rica land use data with environmental and geographic data
method: dynamic model of land use generating estimated deforestation equations
finding: In Costa Rica, a dynamic land use model with estimated deforestation equations showed that susceptibility to deforestation depended on environmental, geographic and socioeconomic characteristics.
gap_quote: In practice, however, several questions have been raised about their feasibility. Therefore, understanding the processes and determinants of land use changes is critical.

title: Prevalence and diversity patterns of avian blood parasites in degraded African rainforest habitats
data: paired disturbed and undisturbed habitat sites
method: paired site sampling, mitochondrial cytochrome b lineage identification, prevalence comparison
predictors: habitat type disturbed or undisturbed, host bird species
finding: In southern Cameroon, Leucocytozoon prevalence in two rainforest birds was 50.3 per cent in undisturbed and 35.8 per cent in deforested habitats, and Plasmodium lineages responded in opposite ways.
gap_quote: Land use changes including deforestation, road construction and agricultural encroachments have been linked to the increased prevalence of several infectious diseases.

title: Assessment of Land Cover Change in Peri-Urban High Andean Environments South of Bogotá, Colombia
place: Colombia, Rio Tunjuelo basin south of Bogotá
data: not stated
method: random forest classification, multiple logistic regression
predictors: distance to established agricultural areas, environmental parameters
finding: In the Rio Tunjuelo basin over 1989 to 2016, urban spread slowed, farmland grew and natural vegetation shrank, its change likelier near farmland, though explained deviance stayed low.
gap_quote: Since Bogotá is steadily growing, the city spreads into its peri-urban area, thus threatening its proximal ecosystems.

title: Questioning emissions-based approaches for the definition of REDD+ deforestation baselines in high forest cover/low deforestation countries
data: not stated
method: deforestation scenarios from historical-trend methods to explicit modelling with socio-economic variables
predictors: socio-economic variables at the regional scale
validation: scenarios compared with each other and with the existing socio-economic situation
finding: In the Guiana Shield, common baseline methods predicted huge deforestation increases unlikely under existing socio-economic conditions, and funds under most scenarios were unlikely to cover avoided deforestation costs.
gap_quote: REDD+ is being questioned by the particular status of High Forest/Low Deforestation countries. Indeed, the formulation of reference levels is made difficult by the confrontation of low historical deforestation records with the forest transition theory on the one hand. On the other hand, those countries might formulate incredibly high deforestation scenarios to ensure large payments even in case of inaction.

title: Targeted carbon conservation at national scales with high-resolution monitoring
data: new high-resolution aboveground carbon map, maps of ecosystem threats and protections
method: high-resolution carbon mapping overlaid with ecosystem threats and protections
predictors: current ecosystem threats, protections, natural controls over carbon density
finding: In Peru, at least 0.8 Pg of aboveground carbon was at imminent risk of emission from land use, and three biogeographic strategies could fully offset these emissions.
gap_quote: Yet, the geographically complex mosaic of threats to, and opportunities for, conserving carbon in landscapes remain largely unresolved at national scales.

title: Evidence that a national REDD+ program reduces tree cover loss and carbon emissions in a high forest cover, low deforestation country
period: 2010 to 2015 and after payments ended, other years not stated
data: annual tree cover loss data, product not stated
method: synthetic matching to build a counterfactual tree cover loss trajectory
finding: The Norway and Guyana REDD+ program cut tree cover loss 35 per cent over 2010 to 2015, avoiding 12.8 million tons of CO2, but loss rose after payments ended.
gap_quote: However, we found that tree cover loss increased after the payments ended, and therefore, our results suggest that without continued payments, forest protection is not guaranteed.

title: Anthropogenic modification of forests means only 40% of remaining forests have high ecosystem integrity
data: observed and inferred human pressure data, a lost connectivity index, forest extent data not named
method: integration of human pressures and lost connectivity into a continuous forest condition index
finding: Only 40.5 per cent of forest, 17.4 million km2, had high landscape integrity, mostly in Canada, Russia, the Amazon, Central Africa and New Guinea, with 27 per cent protected.
gap_quote: Many global environmental agendas, including halting biodiversity loss, reversing land degradation, and limiting climate change, depend upon retaining forests with high ecological integrity, yet the scale and degree of forest modification remain poorly quantified and mapped.

title: The nexus between forest fragmentation in Africa and Ebola virus disease outbreaks
data: land cover change data, Ebola virus disease outbreak records
method: association of outbreak index cases with forest fragmentation hotspots
finding: Index cases of Ebola virus disease outbreaks in West and Central Africa over 2004 to 2014 occurred mostly in hotspots of forest fragmentation.
gap_quote: Human populations living close to forest margins fragmented and disturbed by deforestation may be particularly exposed to zoonotic infections because of the higher likelihood for humans to be in contact with disease reservoirs. Quantitative analysis of the nexus between deforestation and the emergence of Ebola virus disease (EVD), however, is still missing.

title: Protected Areas' Impacts Upon Land Cover Within Mexico: the need to add politics and dynamics to static land-use economics
data: not stated
method: static land-use economic baselines for protected area impact estimation, initial political economy model
predictors: protected area type and strictness, proximity to cities
finding: Mexican protected areas lowered natural land cover loss by 2.5 per cent over 2000 to 2005, stricter ones 4.4 against 2.3 per cent, which static baselines did not explain.
gap_quote: Given this point − now often included in impact evaluation via matching − further theory is required to explain variations in policy impact.

title: Variability of soil organic carbon and nutrient content across land uses and agriculturally induced land use changes in the forest-savanna transition zone of Cameroon
data: nine land uses identified in the study area, soil samples at 0 to 10 and 10 to 30 cm
method: soil sampling in three replicates per land use with physicochemical analysis and significance tests
predictors: land use, direction of land use change, soil depth
finding: Soil organic carbon stocks were highest under native forest and forest-based cocoa agroforestry, 32.1 to 27.8 Mg per ha, and changed significantly mainly where native savannah became cropland.
gap_quote: Data expressing the effects of land use change on soil attributes is still very scarce in Cameroon as in most of Africa.

title: The Conservation atlas of tropical forests
data: IUCN maps of African rain forests
method: compilation of rain forest maps and country studies
finding: IUCN released an atlas of African rain forest maps with country studies, analysing the extent and causes of deforestation and the future of Africa's tropical forests.
gap_quote: Recognizing that sound information is vital to the progress of conservation, IUCN have gathered together a visual portfolio of maps of rain forests in Africa.

title: How Climate Change and Land Use/Land Cover Change Affect Domestic Water Vulnerability in Yangambi Watersheds (D. R. Congo)
place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Yangambi Biosphere Reserve watersheds

finding: In Yangambi, land cover indices significantly influenced water quality, with edge density of perturbed forest explaining up to 94 per cent of pH variation.
gap_quote: Surprisingly, given its proximity to the Congo River, the YBR is confronted with water issues. As part of its ecosystem function, the landscape is expected to reduce deterioration of water quality. However, environmental consequences are increasing due to conversion of its dense forest into other types of land use/land cover (LULC) in response to human activities.

title: Quantification of global gross forest cover loss
data: satellite imagery
method: globally consistent satellite-based estimation of gross forest cover loss
finding: Gross forest cover loss in 2000 to 2005 was 1,011,000 km2, 3.1 per cent of forest, and among large forest countries proportionally least in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
gap_quote: However, GFCL represents only one component of net change, and the processes driving GFCL and rates of recovery from GFCL differ regionally.

title: CONSERVING TROPICAL RAIN FORESTS IN INDONESIA: A QUANTITATIVE ASSESSMENT OF ALTERNATIVE POLICIES
data: not stated

finding: In an Indonesian general equilibrium model, raising the minimum harvest age was the best forestry policy, wood import restrictions were ineffective and costly, and compensation payments could offset conservation losses.
gap_quote: At the global level, import restrictions, for Indonesian wood products are ecologically ineffective and place considerable costs on the Indonesian economy, whereas compensation payments can compensate for the losses of forest conservation, if the money is invested in the creation of new employment opportunities.

title: Biodiversity co‐benefits of reducing emissions from deforestation under alternative reference levels and levels of finance
data: not stated

title: Unveiling small-scale tropical forest loss and post-loss recovery in the Congo Basin
data: Landsat and Sentinel-2 records, Global Forest Change and JRC tropical moist forest products for comparison

gap_quote: Despite containing the world’s second-largest tropical forest, the nuances of forest dynamics in the Congo Basin remain relatively less studied compared to other major tropical regions.

title: Tropical forest cover change in the 1990s and options for future monitoring
data: FAO Forest Resources Assessment 2000, TREES II, Earth observing satellite imagery

finding: Humid tropics lost about 5.8 Mha of forest yearly in the 1990s, Africa's humid forests 0.4 to 0.5 per cent yearly, and country statistics differed from satellite estimates in Africa.
gap_quote: Despite the importance of the world's humid tropical forests, our knowledge concerning their rates of change remains limited.

title: Deforestation in the Brazilian Amazon: Comparing the Impacts of Macroeconomic Shocks, Land Tenure, and Technological Change
data: not stated

predictors: real exchange rate, agricultural tax and support policies, transportation costs from infrastructure investment, land tenure regimes, technological change in agriculture

title: Identifying Drivers and Spatial Patterns of Deforestation in the Rio Grande Basin, Colombia
data: land cover from Landsat TM and ETM imagery

gap_quote: Identifying the spatial patterns and drivers of deforestation is a critical task in geographic research. In addition to mapping deforestation, it’s important to determine the statistical effects of the spatial configuration of tropical landscapes on current deforestation trends.

title: Losing connection: The decline of structurally intact forests linking protected areas in West Africa

title: Agriculture, Ecosystem Functions, and Services in the Congo Basin
data: not stated
